title: Inventory Restock Planner
spec: `restock(inventory)` Takes a list of tuples containing an item name, current quantity, and daily sales. Calculate how many days until the item runs out. If it runs out in under seven days, calculate the amount needed to restock to a thirty day supply. Return a list of tuples with item names and restock amounts, omitting items that do not need restocking.

title: Text Word Wrapper
spec: `wrap(words, limit)` Takes a list of words and a maximum line width. Greedily pack words into lines such that the length of the words plus the necessary single spaces between them does not exceed the limit. If a single word is longer than the limit, place it on its own line. Return a list of strings representing the formatted lines.

title: Run Length Codec
spec: `compress(sequence)` Perform run length encoding on a string of alphabetic characters by counting consecutive identical characters and formatting them as the character followed by the count. Also implement a separate decoding function that expands the compressed format back to the original text. The main function must compress the input and return the compressed string. Example input of aabbbc yields a2b3c.

title: Moving Average Crossover
spec: `crossover(prices)` Takes a list of daily closing prices. Compute a three day simple moving average and a seven day simple moving average. Find all days starting from the seventh day where the three day average crosses above the seven day average. Return a list of integers representing the zero indexed days where this upward crossover occurs.

title: Sudoku Grid Validator
spec: `validate(grid)` Takes a list of nine lists, each containing nine integers representing a board. Check if every row and every column contains the numbers one through nine exactly once without repetition. Ignore the three by three subgrids for this specific exercise. Return a boolean indicating whether the rows and columns are entirely valid.

title: Bowling Score Calculator
spec: `score(rolls)` Takes a list of integers representing pins knocked down in a game of tenpin bowling. Calculate the total score for all ten frames, handling strikes and spares according to standard rules. A strike adds the next two rolls as a bonus, and a spare adds the next one roll as a bonus. Return the final integer score.

title: Bracket Matcher
spec: `balance(expression)` Takes a string containing various parentheses, curly braces, and square brackets along with other characters. Scan the string to verify that all opening brackets are properly closed in the correct order by their corresponding closing brackets. Return a boolean true if they are balanced, and false otherwise.

title: Poker Hand Evaluator
spec: `evaluate(hand)` Takes a list of five strings, where each string is a two character representation of a playing card with rank and suit. Determine the rank of the hand by checking for a flush, a straight, three of a kind, pairs, or a high card. Return an integer score from one to five where five represents a straight flush and one represents just a high card.

title: Word Frequency Histogram
spec: `histogram(text)` Takes a paragraph of text. Convert it to lowercase and remove all punctuation. Count the frequency of each word. Return a list of tuples containing the word and its count, sorted by the count in descending order, and then alphabetically for ties.

title: Maze Pathfinder
spec: `navigate(maze)` Takes a list of lists of integers representing a grid where zero is open space and one is a wall. Find the shortest path from the top left corner to the bottom right corner using breadth first search. Return the number of steps in the shortest path, or negative one if no path exists. Moves can only be horizontal or vertical.

title: Simple Markdown Parser
spec: `parse(document)` Takes a list of strings representing lines of text. Convert lines starting with a hash symbol into heading tags, counting the hashes to determine the heading level. Convert empty lines into paragraph breaks, and wrap contiguous regular lines in paragraph tags. Return a single joined string containing the converted hypertext markup.

title: Matrix Operations
spec: `transform(matrix)` Takes a list of lists representing a square matrix of integers. First, compute the transpose of the matrix. Then, multiply the original matrix by its transpose using standard row by column multiplication. Do not use external math libraries. Return the resulting matrix as a list of lists.

title: IP Address Validator
spec: `validate(address)` Takes a string that may represent an internet protocol version four address. Split it by dots and ensure there are exactly four parts. Check that each part consists only of digits, does not have leading zeroes unless it is exactly zero, and falls in the numerical range zero to two hundred fifty five. Return a boolean true if valid.

title: Log Anomaly Detector
spec: `analyze(logs)` Takes a list of strings where each string contains a timestamp, a user identifier, and an action separated by spaces. Group the actions by user identifier. Count how many times a user performs a failure action within a sliding window of five log entries for that user. If a user has three or more failures in any consecutive five attempts, return their identifier in a list.

title: Dependency Resolver
spec: `resolve(dependencies)` Takes a list of tuples where the first element is a task name and the second is a task it depends on. Perform a topological sort to find a valid execution order for the tasks. If a cycle is detected meaning the tasks cannot be completed, return an empty list. Otherwise, return a list of tasks in the order they should be executed.

title: Anagram Grouper
spec: `group(words)` Takes a list of lowercase string words. Group the words that contain the exact same letters in different orders, ignoring punctuation. Create a list of lists, where each inner list contains words that are anagrams of each other. Filter out any groups that contain only a single word. Return the list of lists sorted by group size.

title: Caesar Cipher Cracker
spec: `crack(ciphertext)` Takes an encrypted string of letters and spaces. Try all twenty five possible alphabetical shifts. For each shift, count how many of the resulting words appear in a minimal internal list of common english words like the, be, to, of, and. Return the decrypted string that yields the highest count of recognized common words.

title: File System Path Simplifier
spec: `simplify(path)` Takes a string representing an absolute file path with slashes, dots, and double dots. Process the path sequentially to resolve the double dots by moving up a directory, and ignore single dots or multiple consecutive slashes. Return the shortest equivalent absolute path string starting with a single slash.

title: Meeting Room Scheduler
spec: `schedule(intervals)` Takes a list of tuples where each tuple has a start integer and an end integer representing meeting times in minutes from midnight. Determine the minimum number of separate conference rooms required to accommodate all meetings without overlap. Return the integer count of required rooms.

title: Roman Numeral Converter
spec: `convert(numeral)` Takes a string representing a valid roman numeral up to three thousand. Iterate through the characters to compute the base ten integer value. If a smaller character appears before a larger one, subtract it instead of adding it. Return the calculated integer. For example, an input of nine in roman format returns nine.

title: Game of Life Simulator
spec: `simulate(grid)` Takes a list of lists of integers representing a grid of living and dead cells. Calculate the next state of the board according to the standard rules of life, where cells survive with two or three neighbors and dead cells become alive with exactly three neighbors. Return a new list of lists representing the next generation.

title: Arithmetic Expression Evaluator
spec: `calculate(expression)` Takes a string containing digits, plus, minus, multiply, and divide characters. Parse and evaluate the expression using standard order of operations without using built in evaluation functions. Assume all inputs are valid and spaces may be present. Return the integer result of the calculation.

title: Text Justification
spec: `justify(words, width)` Takes a list of words and an integer width. Group words into lines such that they fit the width, then distribute extra spaces evenly between the words on each line so the total length exactly matches the width. If spaces cannot be distributed evenly, put the extras on the left. Return a list of justified strings.

title: Pascal Triangle Generator
spec: `generate(rows)` Takes an integer representing the number of rows to produce. Construct the triangle where each number is the sum of the two numbers directly above it from the previous row. The edges are always one. Return a list of lists containing the integers for each row up to the specified count.

title: Version Number Comparator
spec: `compare(versions)` Takes a list of two strings representing software version numbers separated by dots. Split both strings by dots and convert the parts to integers. Compare the components from left to right. Return one if the first version is greater, negative one if the second is greater, and zero if they are strictly equal.

title: Flight Route Cost Calculator
spec: Create a function `optimize(flights, requests)`. The first argument is a list of connections where each item contains a departure city, arrival city, ticket price, and flight duration in minutes. The second argument is a list of desired trips, each containing a starting city and a destination. Build a graph of these connections and use a shortest path algorithm to find the lowest possible total price for each requested trip. If two paths have the identical lowest price, choose the one with the shorter total flight duration. Return a list of tuples containing the lowest price and total duration for each request, or a tuple of negative one and negative one if no route exists. Example input includes a flight from Seattle to Boston costing 300 taking 360 minutes, which would yield an output of 300, 360.

title: Library Penalty Assessor
spec: Write a function `bill(patrons, checkouts)`. The first argument is a list of library members where each item contains a member identifier and a loyalty tier of either basic or premium. The second argument is a list of overdue records containing a member identifier, material category, and days late. Calculate the penalty for each record where books cost fifty cents per day, audio is one dollar per day, and equipment is five dollars per day. Premium members receive a three day grace period where no penalty accrues, but after that they pay the normal rate for all days late. The maximum penalty per item is twenty dollars for books, fifty for audio, and two hundred for equipment. Accumulate the total owed for each member and return a list of tuples containing the member identifier and their total balance.

title: Customer Ticket Escalator
spec: Implement a function `escalate(tickets, agents)`. The first input is a list of support tickets containing a ticket identifier, an issue severity of low, medium, or high, and the number of hours the ticket has been open. The second input is a list of support staff containing an agent identifier, their maximum allowed severity level, and their current active ticket count. Assign each ticket to an agent who is authorized to handle its severity and currently has the fewest active tickets. High severity tickets that have been open for more than four hours must instead be added to a special unassigned priority queue. Return a tuple containing a list of assigned tickets paired with their assigned agent identifier, followed by a list of ticket identifiers in the unassigned priority queue.

title: Subscription Billing Prorater
spec: Create a function `prorate(events)`. The input is a list of customer actions in a single thirty day month, where each item contains a day of the month as an integer, an action type of subscribe, upgrade, downgrade, or cancel, and a daily rate as a float. Customers start the month with no active subscription. Process the events chronologically to determine the active daily rate for each customer on any given day. A customer pays their current active rate for each day until a new event changes it on a subsequent day. If multiple events occur for the same customer on the same day, only the last event dictates the rate going forward. Return a list of tuples containing each unique customer identifier and their total accumulated cost for the thirty day month, rounded to two decimal places.

title: Conveyor Belt Package Router
spec: Develop a function `route(packages)`. The input is a list of parcels where each item contains a tracking number, weight in kilograms, volume in cubic liters, and a boolean flag indicating if it requires priority shipping. Route each parcel to the correct output chute based on its attributes. Parcels weighing more than twenty kilograms or with a volume exceeding one hundred cubic liters must be routed to the heavy freight chute. Of the remaining parcels, those with the priority flag set to true go to the express chute, while all others go to the standard chute. If a parcel is designated for the heavy freight chute but also has the priority flag set, append its tracking number to a special manual review list instead. Return a list containing four lists of tracking numbers in this order: heavy freight, express, standard, and manual review.

title: Recipe Ingredient Scaler
spec: Write a function `scale(recipe, multiplier)`. The first parameter is a list of ingredients where each item contains an ingredient name, a numerical amount, and a unit of measurement such as teaspoon, tablespoon, cup, or ounce. The second parameter is a float representing the scaling factor. Multiply the amount of each ingredient by the scaling factor. After scaling, simplify the units of measurement to the largest possible whole unit without losing precision. For example, if a scaled amount results in three teaspoons, convert it to one tablespoon; if a scaled amount reaches four cups, convert it to one quart. Supported conversions are three teaspoons to one tablespoon, sixteen tablespoons to one cup, and four cups to one quart. Ounces do not convert. Return a list of updated ingredients containing the name, new amount, and new unit.

title: Elevator Simulation Controller
spec: Implement a function `simulate(calls, floors)`. The first argument is a chronological list of passenger requests containing the time in seconds, the origin floor, and the destination floor. The second argument is the highest floor in the building. A single elevator starts at floor one at time zero and moves at a speed of one floor per second. It takes two seconds for passengers to enter or exit, during which the elevator must remain stationary. The elevator always finishes serving all requests in its current direction of travel before reversing direction, picking up any passengers along the way whose origin and destination align with the current path. Calculate the time at which the final passenger arrives at their destination. Return this total elapsed time in seconds.

title: Vending Machine Dispenser
spec: Create a function `dispense(transactions, coins)`. The first argument is a list of purchases where each item contains the cost of an item and the total amount paid by the customer. The second argument is a list of available coins in the machine, starting with their monetary value and the quantity available, sorted from highest value to lowest. For each transaction, calculate the required change and dispense it using a greedy approach, taking from the available coins. Update the available coin quantities after every successful transaction. If the machine cannot provide exact change for a transaction using the available coins, cancel that purchase entirely, keep the coin inventory unchanged, and record the transaction as failed. Return a tuple containing the final updated list of available coins and the total number of failed transactions.

title: Text Sentiment Scorer
spec: Develop a function `score(reviews, lexicon)`. The first input is a list of plain text product reviews. The second input is a list of words paired with an integer sentiment value ranging from negative five to positive five. For each review, split the text into individual lowercase words and remove all punctuation. Sum the sentiment values of the words found in the lexicon. Apply a negation rule where the presence of the word not or never inverts the sign of the sentiment value for the immediately following word, provided that following word exists in the lexicon. Ignore words that do not appear in the lexicon. Return a list of integers representing the final calculated sentiment score for each review. An example input review of not bad where bad has a score of negative three should yield a total score of positive three.

title: Packet Fragment Reassembler
spec: Write a function `reassemble(fragments)`. The input is a list of network packet pieces where each item contains a unique message identifier, a sequence index, the total number of pieces expected for that message, and a string payload. Group the pieces by their message identifier. For each message, check if all expected pieces have been received by comparing the count of unique sequence indices to the total expected pieces. If a message is complete, concatenate the string payloads in ascending order of their sequence indices to form the original text. Discard any messages that are missing one or more pieces. Return a list of tuples containing the message identifier and the reconstructed text, sorted numerically by the message identifier.

title: CPU Task Scheduler
spec: Implement a function `schedule(tasks, quantum)`. The first parameter is a list of processes where each item contains a process identifier, an arrival time in milliseconds, and a total required execution time in milliseconds. The second parameter is the time slice limit in milliseconds for a round robin scheduling algorithm. Simulate the execution of these processes on a single processor. The processor runs an active process for up to the time slice limit before moving it to the back of the waiting queue and loading the next available process. A process only enters the waiting queue once the simulation clock reaches its arrival time. Determine the exact millisecond when each process completely finishes its required execution time. Return a list of tuples pairing each process identifier with its final completion time, sorted chronologically by completion time.

title: Contact List Deduplicator
spec: Create a function `merge(contacts)`. The input is a list of individual records containing a first name, last name, email address, and phone number. Identify duplicate records by assuming that any two records sharing an identical non-empty email address or an identical non-empty phone number belong to the same person. Because these matches can chain together, locate all connected components of duplicate records. For each unified person, create a single merged record by selecting the longest available string for the first name, last name, email address, and phone number from among their duplicate records. If multiple strings have the same longest length, choose the one that appears first alphabetically. Return a list of the fully merged contact records.

title: Pagination Link Generator
spec: Develop a function `paginate(current, total)`. The first argument is the currently active page number as an integer. The second argument is the total number of available pages. Generate a sequence of page numbers to display in a navigation menu. The menu must always include the first page, the last page, the currently active page, and the two pages immediately preceding and following the active page. Any gaps of more than one page between the included numbers must be represented by a string containing three periods. For example, if the current page is five and the total is twenty, the output sequence should be the number one, the periods string, the numbers three, four, five, six, seven, the periods string, and the number twenty. Return the sequence as a list of mixed integers and strings.

title: Sensor Data Smoother
spec: Write a function `filter(readings, window)`. The first input is a chronologically ordered list of floating point temperature readings. The second input is an integer representing the size of a moving historical window. Iterate through the readings starting from the point where a full historical window is available. For each subsequent reading, calculate the mean and standard deviation of the immediately preceding window of readings. If the current reading deviates from the mean by more than two standard deviations, classify it as an anomaly. Replace any anomaly with the median value of its preceding window before continuing, so that the corrected value is used in the history for future calculations. Return a list containing all the readings with the anomalies corrected.

title: Warehouse Bin Packing
spec: Implement a function `pack(items, capacity)`. The first parameter is a list of integers representing the weights of various items needing storage. The second parameter is the maximum weight capacity of a single storage bin. Sort the items in descending order of their weight. Pack them using a first fit approach, placing each item into the oldest created bin that still has enough remaining capacity to hold it. If an item cannot fit into any existing bin, create a new bin at the end of the line and place the item there. Once all items are processed, count how many bins are exactly full, how many are at least half full but not entirely full, and how many are less than half full. Return a tuple containing these three counts in that specific order.

title: Traffic Intersection Director
spec: Create a function `direct(vehicles, duration)`. The first argument is a list of cars arriving at a four-way intersection, where each item contains an arrival time in seconds and an approach direction of north, south, east, or west. The second argument is the total number of seconds to simulate. The traffic light allows north and south traffic to pass for twenty seconds, then switches to allow east and west traffic to pass for twenty seconds. The cycle repeats indefinitely, starting with north and south green at time zero. During a green light, one waiting car from each allowed direction can pass through the intersection every second. A car cannot pass on the exact second it arrives. Return a tuple containing the number of cars that successfully passed through and the total number of cars still waiting in all queues at the end of the duration.

title: Gene Sequence Motif Finder
spec: Develop a function `search(sequence, motifs)`. The first input is a long text string representing a genetic sequence comprised entirely of the letters A, C, G, and T. The second input is a list of short structural patterns to find within the sequence. These patterns may contain standard letters as well as a wildcard character N that can match any single letter. Scan the long genetic string to find every starting index where a pattern appears. Patterns are allowed to overlap with one another. If a pattern does not occur anywhere in the sequence, it should still be included in the results with an empty collection of indices. Return a list of tuples, each pairing the original structural pattern string with a list of zero-based integers representing all its starting indices in the sequence.

title: Cash Flow NPV Calculator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(projects, rate)`. The first argument is a list of investment opportunities where each item contains a project name, an initial negative cash outflow, and a list of projected positive cash inflows for subsequent consecutive years. The second argument is the annual discount rate expressed as a decimal. Calculate the net present value for each project by dividing each year's inflow by one plus the discount rate raised to the power of the year index, then summing those discounted inflows and adding the initial negative outflow. Discard any project whose net present value is less than zero. Sort the remaining profitable projects in descending order based on their net present value. Return a list of the project names that met the criteria.

title: Morse Code Audio Decoder
spec: Implement a function `decode(signal)`. The input is a string of zeroes and ones representing sampled audio of a telegraph transmission. A one represents tone and a zero represents silence. Count the lengths of consecutive identical characters to determine the structure of the message. One unit of tone is a dot, and three consecutive units of tone is a dash. One unit of silence separates parts of the same letter, three units of silence separates different letters, and seven units of silence separates different words. Convert the raw zeroes and ones into a formatted text string where dots are represented by periods, dashes are represented by hyphens, letters are separated by a single space, and words are separated by a forward slash. Return the formatted text string.

title: Chessboard Threat Validator
spec: Create a function `threatens(pieces)`. The input is a list of active chess figures on an eight by eight grid, where each item contains a type of rook, bishop, knight, or queen, followed by a row index and a column index. Evaluate the positions to find every instance where one figure can legally capture another figure based on standard movement rules, ignoring the possibility of figures blocking the path. Rooks move in straight horizontal or vertical lines, bishops move diagonally, queens move in both straight lines and diagonals, and knights move in an L-shape pattern. Two pieces cannot occupy the same square. Return a list of tuples containing the row and column of the attacking figure paired with the row and column of the targeted figure, sorted by the attacker's row.

title: E-commerce Discount Stacker
spec: Develop a function `checkout(cart, coupons)`. The first parameter is a list of prices for items in a shopping basket. The second parameter is a list of available promotional codes containing a discount type of either flat or percentage, a discount numerical value, and a minimum required basket total before the code can be used. Calculate the initial sum of the items in the basket. Determine the best possible final price by applying at most one flat discount and at most one percentage discount. If both are applied, the percentage discount must be calculated on the new total after the flat discount is subtracted. Only promotional codes whose minimum required basket total is met by the initial sum are eligible for use. Return the lowest possible final price rounded to two decimal places.

title: Memory Cache Simulator
spec: Write a function `cache(requests, capacity)`. The first input is a list of string identifiers representing data queries. The second input is the maximum number of items the storage can hold. Simulate a least recently used eviction policy. When a query is made, check if its identifier is already in the storage. If it is present, record a hit and move that identifier to the most recently used position. If it is absent, record a miss and add the identifier to the most recently used position. Whenever adding a new identifier causes the storage to exceed its maximum capacity, remove the identifier that currently occupies the least recently used position. Return a list of boolean values corresponding to the chronological queries, where true indicates a hit and false indicates a miss.

title: Transit Fare Zone Calculator
spec: Implement a function `fare(stations, journeys)`. The first argument is a list of stops where each item contains a stop name and an integer representing its geographic zone. The second argument is a list of passenger trips containing a starting stop name and an ending stop name. The base price for any trip is two dollars and fifty cents. For every zone boundary crossed during the trip, an additional one dollar and twenty five cents is added to the price. The number of boundaries crossed is equal to the absolute difference between the starting stop zone and the ending stop zone. If a starting or ending stop name does not exist in the list of stations, the trip is invalid and its price should be recorded as zero. Return a list of the calculated prices for all the passenger trips.

title: Bank Account Reconciler
spec: Create a function `reconcile(transactions)`. The input is a chronological list of account activities where each item contains an integer month from one to twelve, a description, an amount as a float, and a category of either credit or debit. The account starts with a balance of zero dollars. Process the activities in order, adding credits to the balance and subtracting debits. At the conclusion of each unique month present in the activities, evaluate the balance. If the balance at the end of that month is below five hundred dollars, automatically deduct a ten dollar maintenance fee from the account. Return a tuple containing the final account balance after all months are processed and the total amount of maintenance fees deducted throughout the year.

title: Course Prerequisite Checker
spec: Develop a function `graduate(courses, history)`. The first parameter is a list of degree requirements where each item contains a course code and a list of alternative prerequisite course codes. The second parameter is a list of course codes that a student has already successfully completed. To enroll in a degree requirement, the student must have completed at least one of its listed alternative prerequisites. If a requirement has an empty list of prerequisites, it can be taken immediately. Check each degree requirement against the completed history to determine if the student is eligible to take it. Create two separate lists: one containing the course codes the student is eligible to take, and another containing the course codes they are not yet eligible to take. Return a tuple of these two lists.

title: Dungeon Crawl Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(dungeon)` to process a hero exploring a sequence of rooms. The input is a list of tuples containing a room type as a string, either monster or potion, and an integer value. The hero starts with fifty health. If they encounter a monster, they lose health equal to the value. If they find a potion, they heal by the value up to a strict maximum of fifty. If health drops to zero or below, the run ends immediately and no further rooms are processed. Return a tuple with the final health and the count of cleared rooms. Example input: [("monster", 20), ("potion", 10), ("monster", 50)]. Example output: (0, 2).

title: Tax Bracket Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(incomes)` to determine the tax owed by different individuals. The input is a list of integers representing annual earnings. The rules state that the first ten thousand is completely tax free. Any amount between ten thousand and thirty thousand is taxed at ten percent. Any amount above thirty thousand is taxed at twenty percent. Return a list of total tax owed for each income in the same order, with all values rounded down to the nearest integer. Example input: [5000, 15000, 35000]. Example output: [0, 500, 3000].

title: Pizza Order Pricer
spec: Write a function `price(orders)` to compute the total cost of a pizza delivery. The input is a list of tuples, each containing a size as a string which is small, medium, or large, and a list of string topping names. A small base costs ten, a medium costs twelve, and a large costs fifteen. Each topping adds exactly two to the cost. If an order has three or more toppings on a single pizza, apply a flat discount of five to that specific pizza. Return the total cost of all pizzas combined as an integer. Example input: [("small", ["cheese"]), ("large", ["pepperoni", "mushrooms", "onions"])]. Example output: 28.

title: Ski Resort Lift Pass
spec: Write a function `evaluate(skiers)` to calculate the cost for lift passes. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer age and a number of consecutive days. A standard daily pass costs eighty. Children under twelve pay forty per day, and seniors over sixty five pay fifty per day. Buying three or more consecutive days gives a ten percent discount on the total price for that specific skier. Return a list of the final prices for each skier, rounded down to the nearest integer. Example input: [(10, 1), (30, 4), (70, 2)]. Example output: [40, 288, 100].

title: Hotel Room Assigner
spec: Write a function `assign(groups)` to allocate rooms to arriving guests. The input is a list of integers representing the number of people in each arriving group. The hotel has standard rooms that hold two people and suites that hold four people. Always assign a suite if the group has three or four people. If a group has one or two people, assign a standard room. If a group has more than four people, divide them into the minimum total number of suites and standard rooms required, preferring suites over standard rooms. Return a list of tuples containing the number of suites and standard rooms assigned to each group. Example input: [2, 4, 5]. Example output: [(0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)].

title: Car Rental Quoter
spec: Write a function `quote(rentals)` to estimate prices for renting vehicles. The input is a list of tuples containing a car type as a string which is economy, sedan, or suv, an integer of rental days, and the driver age. Economy costs thirty per day, sedan costs forty, and suv costs fifty. Drivers under twenty five pay a surcharge of fifteen per day. Rentals lasting seven days or longer receive a flat twenty deduction from the final total. Return a list of quoted prices for each rental. Example input: [("economy", 3, 22), ("suv", 7, 40)]. Example output: [135, 330].

title: Board Game Score Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(hands)` to tally points at the end of a card game. The input is a list of player hands, where each hand is a list of string card types which can be farmer, noble, or merchant. Each farmer is worth two points and each noble is worth five points. A merchant is normally worth one point, but if a single hand contains at least one of all three types, every merchant in that hand becomes worth three points instead. Return a list of total scores for each hand. Example input: [["farmer", "farmer"], ["merchant", "farmer", "noble", "merchant"]]. Example output: [4, 13].

title: Coffee Shop Barista
spec: Write a function `brew(orders)` to process a line of drink requests. The input is a list of string drink names which can be espresso, latte, or mocha. The shop begins with ten units of beans, five units of milk, and two units of chocolate. An espresso uses one bean. A latte uses one bean and one milk. A mocha uses one bean, one milk, and one chocolate. Process the orders sequentially. If there are not enough ingredients for a drink, skip it entirely and check the next one. Return a tuple containing the integer count of successfully brewed drinks and a tuple of the remaining units of beans, milk, and chocolate. Example input: ["mocha", "mocha", "mocha", "espresso"]. Example output: (3, (7, 3, 0)).

title: Payroll Overtime Tracker
spec: Write a function `payroll(timesheets)` to compute weekly wages. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer hourly rate and a list of seven integers representing hours worked each day from Monday to Sunday. The standard rate applies up to forty total hours for the week. Any hours beyond forty are paid at one point five times the standard rate. However, any hours worked on the seventh day are always paid at double the standard rate, and do not count towards the forty hour standard limit. Return a list of total pay for each timesheet, rounded down to the nearest integer. Example input: [(20, [8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 0, 0]), (10, [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8])]. Example output: [800, 160].

title: Theme Park Ticketing
spec: Write a function `ticket(guests)` to calculate total admission revenue. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer age and a height in inches. A base ticket costs fifty. Children under ten pay a reduced price of thirty. Guests must be at least forty eight inches tall to access the main rollercoasters. If they are too short, they receive a ten unit discount on their ticket price. Seniors over sixty pay a flat twenty regardless of their height, and no other discounts apply to them. Return the integer total revenue collected for all guests. Example input: [(8, 45), (25, 60), (65, 55)]. Example output: 90.

title: Supermarket Checkout Scanner
spec: Write a function `checkout(cart)` to process a list of scanned groceries. The input is a list of string item names which are apple, banana, or bread. An apple costs two, a banana costs one, and bread costs three. For apples, a buy one get one free offer applies. For bananas, buying three or more reduces the price to half per banana for all bananas in the cart. Calculate the total cost of the cart, taking these rules into account. Return the final price rounded down to the nearest integer. Example input: ["apple", "apple", "apple", "banana", "banana", "banana", "bread"]. Example output: 8.

title: Fitness Class Booker
spec: Write a function `book(requests)` to manage signups for a studio session. The input is a list of string member types, either vip or regular, wanting to join a class that has a strict maximum capacity of five. VIP members always bypass regular members in the queue, pushing them further back. If the class becomes full, any subsequent members are added to a waitlist. Return a tuple of two lists: the members accepted into the class, and those remaining on the waitlist, preserving the priority order for the accepted list and the original order for the waitlist. Example input: ["regular", "regular", "vip", "regular", "vip", "regular", "regular"]. Example output: (["vip", "vip", "regular", "regular", "regular"], ["regular", "regular"]).

title: Parking Garage Biller
spec: Write a function `bill(sessions)` to calculate fees for a parking structure. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer of hours parked and a boolean indicating if the session occurred on a weekend. The base weekday rate is five per hour. On weekends, the rate increases to seven per hour. There is a daily maximum cap of thirty on weekdays and forty on weekends, meaning a session cannot exceed these amounts. Calculate the fee for each session and return a list of integer fees. Example input: [(2, False), (10, False), (6, True)]. Example output: [10, 30, 40].

title: Bakery Production Planner
spec: Write a function `plan(orders)` to determine baking requirements. The input is a list of string requests for either bread, cake, or pastry. A single batch of bread yields ten loaves and takes two hours to bake. A single batch of cake yields four cakes and takes three hours. A single batch of pastry yields twenty units and takes one hour. Count the total items needed across all orders, then determine the minimum integer number of full batches required for each type to meet the demand. Return a tuple with the total baking hours required and another tuple containing the leftover unused loaves, cakes, and pastries in that order. Example input: ["bread", "bread", "cake", "bread", "cake", "cake", "pastry"]. Example output: (6, (7, 2, 19)).

title: Spacecraft Fuel Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(maneuvers)` to track resource usage during a space flight. The input is a list of tuples containing a string action which can be thrust, rotate, or stabilize, and an integer duration in seconds. A thrust uses ten units of fuel per second. A rotate uses two units per second. Stabilize uses one unit per second. The spacecraft starts with exactly one thousand fuel units. Process the maneuvers in sequential order. If a maneuver requires more fuel than is currently available, skip it and all remaining maneuvers immediately. Return a tuple with the count of successful maneuvers and the remaining fuel balance. Example input: [("thrust", 50), ("rotate", 100), ("thrust", 100)]. Example output: (2, 300).

title: Courier Delivery Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate(packages)` to predict transit times for shipments. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer distance in miles, weight in pounds, and a boolean flag for priority shipping. Standard delivery takes one day for every full or partial hundred miles. Priority shipping halves the total distance based delivery time, rounding up. Any package weighing over fifty pounds adds an extra mandatory day of processing time. If the distance is over one thousand miles, add an extra two days for long haul transit. Return a list of estimated days for each package, rounded up to the nearest whole day. Example input: [(250, 10, False), (400, 60, True), (1200, 20, False)]. Example output: [3, 3, 14].

title: Movie Theater Seating
spec: Write a function `seat(groups)` to assign places to arriving viewers. The input is a list of integers representing group sizes. The theater has five rows with exactly ten seats each. Place each group in the first available row that can fit the entire group together. If a single group is larger than ten, skip them entirely. If no single row has enough adjacent empty seats to fit a group, they are turned away and skipped. Return a tuple containing the integer number of groups successfully seated and the total number of empty seats remaining across the entire theater. Example input: [4, 5, 2, 8]. Example output: (4, 31).

title: Restaurant Tip Splitter
spec: Write a function `split(shifts)` to distribute collected gratuities. The input is a list of tuples containing a string employee role which is server, bartender, or busser, and an integer of hours worked. The total available tip pool is always exactly five hundred. Servers get a multiplier of two, bartenders get one point five, and bussers get one. Calculate each employee share based on their hours multiplied by their role multiplier, then divided by the total weighted hours across all staff. Return a list of integer shares for each employee, rounded down to the nearest whole number. Example input: [("server", 5), ("busser", 10), ("bartender", 4)]. Example output: [192, 192, 115].

title: Escape Room Scorer
spec: Write a function `rank(teams)` to determine the winners of a puzzle challenge. The input is a list of tuples containing a string team name, integer minutes taken, and integer clues used. Every team starts with one thousand points. They lose ten points for every minute taken and fifty points for every clue used. If a team finishes in under thirty minutes, they earn a two hundred point speed bonus. Return a list of team names ordered from highest final score to lowest final score. Example input: [("alpha", 45, 2), ("beta", 25, 3)]. Example output: ["beta", "alpha"].

title: Garden Planting Layout
spec: Write a function `plant(seeds)` to simulate filling a raised dirt bed. The input is a list of string plant types which can be tomato, carrot, or bean. A single garden bed has space for exactly eight units. A tomato requires three units of space, a carrot requires one unit, and a bean requires two units. Add plants to the bed in the exact order they appear in the list until the next plant in the sequence cannot fit. The remaining plants are not planted. Return a tuple containing the integer count of planted seeds and the count of seeds left over. Example input: ["tomato", "bean", "tomato", "carrot", "bean"]. Example output: (3, 2).

title: Pet Boarding Feeder
spec: Write a function `feed(pets)` to calculate daily kibble requirements. The input is a list of tuples containing a string species which is either dog or cat, and an integer weight in pounds. Cats need one cup of food for every full five pounds of body weight. Dogs need one cup for every full ten pounds, plus an extra cup if they weigh over fifty pounds. Return a tuple with the total cups of cat food and total cups of dog food needed for the day. Example input: [("cat", 10), ("dog", 30), ("dog", 60)]. Example output: (2, 10).

title: Trivia Game Moderator
spec: Write a function `moderate(answers)` to score a single player run. The input is a list of booleans representing correct and incorrect answers in sequence. Each correct answer is initially worth ten points. If the player gets three correct answers in a row, every subsequent consecutive correct answer is worth twenty points instead of ten. An incorrect answer awards no points, deducts five points from the total score, and resets the streak count to zero. Return the final integer score. Example input: [True, True, True, True, False, True]. Example output: 45.

title: Music Playlist Curator
spec: Write a function `curate(songs)` to build an optimal listening queue. The input is a list of tuples containing a string song title, a string genre, and an integer duration in minutes. The goal is to build a playlist that does not exceed sixty minutes total. Attempt to add songs in the exact order provided. If adding a song exceeds the time limit, skip it and evaluate the next one. Additionally, never add a song if its genre matches the genre of the immediately preceding song in the playlist. Return a list of the successfully selected song titles. Example input: [("a", "pop", 20), ("b", "pop", 15), ("c", "rock", 30), ("d", "jazz", 15)]. Example output: ["a", "c"].

title: Camping Gear Packer
spec: Write a function `pack(campers)` to determine supply needs for a wilderness trip. The input is a list of tuples containing a string diet which is vegan, vegetarian, or standard, and an integer age. For every two people, rounding up, one tent is required. For every camper under eighteen, one extra sleeping pad is required. For food, each standard camper needs two meat portions. Each vegetarian needs two veggie portions. Each vegan needs three vegan portions. Additionally, every camper over sixty requires a specialized back brace. Return a tuple containing the total integer number of tents, sleeping pads, meat portions, veggie portions, vegan portions, and back braces. Example input: [("standard", 15), ("vegan", 65), ("vegetarian", 30)]. Example output: (2, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1).

title: Art Gallery Appraiser
spec: Write a function `appraise(artworks)` to estimate the value of a collection. The input is a list of tuples containing a string artist name, a string medium which is painting, sculpture, or photograph, and an integer age in years. A painting has a base value of one thousand, a sculpture five hundred, and a photograph two hundred. If the artwork is older than fifty years, its base value doubles. If the artist is exactly the string vangogh, add an extra ten thousand to the value after applying any age multipliers. Return a list of final values for each artwork in the same order. Example input: [("smith", "painting", 10), ("vangogh", "painting", 60)]. Example output: [1000, 12000].

title: Cargo Ship Weight Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(manifests)` that distributes cargo containers into ship bays. The input is a list of tuples containing container identifier, weight, and priority level. The ship has three bays, each with a maximum weight capacity of five thousand units. Place containers into the first available bay that can hold the weight, processing highest priority containers first. If priorities are equal, process heavier containers first. Return a list of three lists, where each inner list contains the identifiers of the containers loaded into that bay in the order they were loaded.

title: Tournament Round Robin Standings
spec: Write a function `evaluate(matches)` that calculates final standings for a sports league. The input is a list of match results, where each result is a tuple of team one name, team two name, team one score, and team two score. A win is worth three points, a draw is one point, and a loss is zero points. Calculate total points and goal difference for each team. Return a list of team names sorted by total points in descending order, using goal difference as a tiebreaker, and alphabetical order as the final tiebreaker.

title: Hospital Triage Queue Priority
spec: Write a function `triage(patients)` that orders a waiting room queue. The input is a list of tuples containing patient name, age, severity score from one to ten, and arrival time in minutes. Sort the patients primarily by severity in descending order. If the severity is identical, prioritize vulnerable ages, meaning children under twelve and seniors over sixty five. If a tie still exists, prioritize the patient with the earlier arrival time. Return a list of patient names in the order they should be seen by the medical staff.

title: Forest Fire Spread Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(grid)` that models a forest fire over a single time step. The input is a list of strings representing a two dimensional grid where a tree is represented by the letter T, a fire by the letter F, and empty space by a period. A tree catches fire if it is adjacent horizontally or vertically to at least one fire. A fire turns into empty space after one step. Empty spaces remain empty. Return a new list of strings representing the grid state after these rules have been applied.

title: Retail Shelf Space Optimizer
spec: Write a function `optimize(products)` that selects items to display on a store shelf of width one hundred. The input is a list of tuples containing product name, width in centimeters, and expected profit. To maximize returns, sort the products by their profit to width ratio in descending order. Iterate through the sorted products and add them to the shelf as long as their width does not exceed the remaining shelf space. Return a list of the names of the products chosen for display.

title: Drone Flight Battery Estimator
spec: Write a function `route(waypoints)` that calculates the energy consumed by a drone flight. The input is a list of tuples containing three dimensional coordinates representing x, y, and altitude. The drone starts with a full battery of one thousand units. Moving horizontally uses one unit of energy per unit of distance. Ascending uses two units per unit of altitude gained, while descending recovers half a unit of energy per unit of altitude lost. Calculate the energy changes between consecutive waypoints. Return a tuple containing the final battery level and a boolean indicating if the drone runs out of power before finishing the route.

title: Real Estate Property Valuer
spec: Write a function `estimate(properties)` that calculates approximate house prices. The input is a list of tuples containing house identifier, base value, number of bedrooms, number of bathrooms, and age in years. Add ten thousand to the base value for each bedroom and five thousand for each bathroom. Deduct one thousand for each year of age, up to a maximum deduction of fifty thousand. If the house has more than four bedrooms, add an extra luxury bonus of twenty thousand. Return a list of tuples containing the house identifier and the final calculated price.

title: Airport Runway Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(flights)` that allocates landing slots. The input is a list of tuples containing flight number, requested arrival time, and fuel emergency status. The runway can handle one landing every five minutes. Sort the flights by requested arrival time. If two flights request the same time or overlap within the five minute window, the flight with a fuel emergency lands first. If both or neither have an emergency, the one with the smaller flight number lands first. Return a list of tuples with flight number and their assigned landing time.

title: Utility Grid Power Distribution
spec: Write a function `distribute(demands)` that allocates electricity from a central power plant with a total capacity of fifty thousand megawatts. The input is a list of tuples containing city name, distance from the plant, and requested power. Sort the cities by distance in ascending order to minimize transmission loss. Allocate the requested power to each city until the plant reaches its capacity. If a city cannot receive its full request, give it the remaining available power. Return a list of tuples containing the city name and the amount of power it received.

title: Stock Portfolio Rebalancer
spec: Write a function `rebalance(holdings)` that determines how many shares to buy or sell. The input is a list of tuples containing stock ticker, current shares, current price, and target allocation percentage. Calculate the total value of the portfolio by summing the product of shares and price for all stocks. For each stock, determine its target value by multiplying the total portfolio value by its target percentage divided by one hundred. Find the difference between the target value and current value, then divide by the current price to get the number of shares to trade, rounding to the nearest integer. Return a list of tuples with the ticker and the share change.

title: Coastal Tide Level Predictor
spec: Write a function `predict(measurements)` that identifies local high and low tides. The input is a list of water level readings taken at hourly intervals. A reading is considered a high tide if it is strictly greater than the reading immediately before and the reading immediately after it. A reading is a low tide if it is strictly less than both its neighbors. The first and last readings cannot be high or low tides. Return a list of tuples containing the index of the tide, the string high or low, and the water level at that hour.

title: Wildlife Migration Distance Tracker
spec: Write a function `track(movements)` that calculates the total distance traveled by tagged animals. The input is a list of tuples containing animal identifier, x coordinate, and y coordinate, ordered by time. Calculate the Euclidean distance between consecutive points for each unique animal identifier. Ignore points where the animal did not move at all. If an animal travels a total distance greater than one hundred units, classify it as migratory. Return a list of identifiers for all migratory animals, sorted alphabetically.

title: Greenhouse Irrigation Scheduler
spec: Write a function `water(sensors)` that determines how many minutes to run sprinklers in different greenhouse zones. The input is a list of tuples containing zone identifier, current soil moisture percentage, and target moisture percentage. For each zone, if the current moisture is greater than or equal to the target, the watering time is zero. Otherwise, calculate the deficit. It takes two minutes of watering to increase the moisture by one percent. If the deficit is greater than twenty percent, add an extra five minutes of soaking time. Return a list of tuples with the zone identifier and the calculated watering time.

title: Railway Ticket Refund Calculator
spec: Write a function `refund(cancellations)` that computes the money to return to passengers. The input is a list of tuples containing passenger name, ticket price, days until departure, and reason for cancellation. If the reason is medical, return the full ticket price regardless of timing. Otherwise, if the cancellation is more than fourteen days before departure, return ninety percent of the price. If it is between three and fourteen days, return fifty percent. Cancellations less than three days before departure receive no refund. Return a list of tuples with the passenger name and their refund amount rounded to two decimal places.

title: Parliamentary Seat Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(votes)` that distributes legislative seats using a proportional method. The input is a list of tuples containing party name and total votes received. The parliament has exactly fifty seats to fill. In each round, calculate a quotient for each party by dividing their total votes by the number of seats they have already been allocated plus one. Award one seat to the party with the highest quotient. Repeat this process until all fifty seats are assigned. Return a list of tuples with the party name and their final seat count, excluding parties that won zero seats.

title: Video Subtitle Time Shifter
spec: Write a function `format(subtitles)` that delays or advances subtitle timestamps. The input is a list of tuples containing a start time in seconds, an end time in seconds, and the subtitle text. Additionally, there is a global delay variable representing seconds to add, which can be negative. Add the delay to both start and end times. If any shifted time falls below zero, clamp it to exactly zero. If the start time equals the end time after clamping, remove that subtitle entry completely. Return a list of the modified tuples.

title: Gymnastics Event Scoring
spec: Write a function `score(routines)` that evaluates athletic performances. The input is a list of tuples containing athlete name, difficulty multiplier, and a list of five judge scores. For each routine, discard the single highest and single lowest judge scores. Calculate the arithmetic mean of the remaining three scores. Multiply this mean by the difficulty multiplier to determine the final score. Return a list of tuples containing the athlete name and their final score rounded to three decimal points, sorted from highest final score to lowest.

title: Insurance Claim Processor
spec: Write a function `process(claims)` that calculates payouts for medical bills. The input is a list of tuples containing policyholder name, procedure cost, deductible amount, and maximum coverage limit. For each claim, subtract the deductible from the procedure cost. If the result is negative, the payout is zero. If the result exceeds the maximum coverage limit, the payout is capped at the limit. Otherwise, the payout is the result. Sum the payouts for each unique policyholder and return a list of tuples with the name and total payout amount.

title: Asteroid Collision Simulator
spec: Write a function `collide(asteroids)` that models space rocks moving in a single dimension. The input is a list of integers representing asteroids, where the absolute value is the size and the sign indicates direction. Positive means moving right, negative means moving left. Asteroids moving in the same direction never collide. If a right moving asteroid meets a left moving one, the smaller one explodes. If they are the same size, both explode. Process all collisions and return a list of the surviving asteroids in their original relative order.

title: Author Royalty Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(sales)` that computes earnings from book purchases. The input is a list of tuples containing author name, book price, and number of copies sold. Royalties are calculated on a tiered system based on copies sold. The first one thousand copies earn ten percent of the book price. Copies sold between one thousand and five thousand earn twelve percent. Any copies sold beyond five thousand earn fifteen percent. Calculate the total royalty for each author and return a list of tuples with the author name and their total earnings.

title: Grid Robot Path Tracer
spec: Write a function `steer(commands)` that tracks a robot moving on a two dimensional grid. The robot starts at coordinates zero and zero, facing north. The input is a list of command strings which can be forward, left, or right. The forward command moves the robot one unit in its current facing direction. Left and right rotate the facing direction by ninety degrees without moving. Process all commands and keep track of every coordinate the robot visits. Return a tuple containing the maximum and minimum x and y coordinates reached to define the bounding box of its path.

title: Email Spam Score Evaluator
spec: Write a function `filter(emails)` that flags suspicious messages. The input is a list of tuples containing sender address, subject line, and message body. Check the subject and body for suspicious words like urgent, winner, and wire. Add one point to the spam score for every occurrence of a suspicious word. If the sender address ends in a reputable domain like dot edu or dot gov, subtract two points from the total score. If the final score is three or greater, classify the email as spam. Return a list of tuples containing the sender address and a boolean indicating if it is spam.

title: Password Strength Validator
spec: Write a function `audit(passwords)` that evaluates the security of user credentials. The input is a list of password strings. A password must be at least eight characters long to be considered valid. To achieve strong status, it must contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special symbol. If a password is valid but misses any of the character type requirements, it is considered medium. Passwords shorter than eight characters are weak. Return a list of strings categorizing each password as weak, medium, or strong.

title: Historical Currency Converter
spec: Write a function `convert(transactions)` that calculates the total value of foreign purchases. The input is a list of tuples containing purchase amount, local currency code, and exchange rate to the base currency. Multiply the purchase amount by the exchange rate to get the base currency value. If the local currency code is not the string USD, apply a foreign transaction fee of two percent to this value. Sum the total converted amounts and fees for all transactions. Return a tuple containing the total base currency value and the total fees collected, both rounded to two decimal places.

title: Algorithmic Melody Sequencer
spec: Write a function `synthesize(pattern)` that generates a sequence of musical notes. The input is a list of integers representing step intervals, and a starting note frequency of four hundred and forty hertz. For each step interval, multiply the previous frequency by a fixed ratio of one point zero six. If the interval is negative, divide by the ratio instead. If the resulting frequency drops below two hundred hertz, double it to raise the octave. If it exceeds eight hundred hertz, halve it. Return a list of the generated frequencies rounded to the nearest integer.

title: Train Carriage Sorter
spec: Write a function `shunt(carriages)` to arrange train carriages. The input is a list of integers representing the destination zones of train carriages in their initial order. The goal is to sort them using a siding track, which acts as a stack. Iterate through the incoming carriages and push them to the siding if their destination zone is strictly less than the one currently at the end of the sorted departure track. Otherwise, move carriages from the siding to the departure track until the condition is met, then push the new carriage. Return a tuple containing the final sorted list of carriages and the maximum number of carriages held in the siding at any one time. Example: input [3, 1, 2] returns a tuple of [1, 2, 3] and 2.

title: Aquarium Water Filter
spec: Implement `simulate(readings)` to track toxicity. The input is a list of tuples containing daily fish waste production and filter operating hours. The tank starts with zero ammonia and a clean filter. Each day, ammonia increases by the waste amount and decreases by the filter hours multiplied by two, but ammonia cannot drop below zero. If the filter operates for more than eight hours in a day, its capacity degrades, reducing its multiplier by a tenth for all future days. If ammonia exceeds ten at the end of any day, the simulation stops immediately. Return the final ammonia level rounded to one decimal place.

title: Mining Claim Assayer
spec: Create a function `evaluate(grid)` for geological analysis. The input is a list of lists of integers representing ore concentrations in a grid. The process must find all three by three subgrids that contain no zero values and have a center value greater than fifty. For each qualifying subgrid, calculate its total ore sum. Return a list of tuples containing the row and column index of the center of each valid subgrid, sorted in descending order by their total ore sum. If multiple subgrids have the same sum, sort them by row index and then column index in ascending order. Example: a uniform grid of nines yields an empty list.

title: Voting Booth Tabulator
spec: Implement `tabulate(ballots)` to resolve an election. The input is a list of lists of strings, where each inner list represents a voter's ranked choice of candidates. In each round of counting, tally the first preference of every ballot that has not been exhausted. If a candidate receives strictly more than half of the active votes, return their name as the winner. Otherwise, find the candidate with the fewest votes, eliminate them from all ballots, and repeat the process. If multiple candidates tie for the fewest votes, eliminate the one whose name comes first alphabetically. Return a string stating the winner or the word tie if all ballots exhaust.

title: Ice Cream Truck Router
spec: Write a function `route(neighborhoods)` to manage a delivery path. The input is a list of tuples containing a neighborhood name, a distance from the previous stop, and an expected customer count. The truck starts with two hundred ice creams and travels to each neighborhood in order. At each stop, subtract the distance traveled from a daily fuel limit of fifty. If the fuel drops below zero, the route terminates early. Serve customers one ice cream each until the inventory runs out, skipping any unserved customers at that stop. Return a list of tuples detailing the neighborhood name and the exact number of ice creams sold there.

title: Telescope Alignment
spec: Create a function `align(targets)` to move a telescope. The input is a list of tuples containing the right ascension and declination of celestial objects in degrees. The telescope starts at coordinates zero zero. For each target, calculate the shortest angular movement required for both axes, wrapping around at three hundred sixty degrees for right ascension. Accumulate the absolute total movement for both axes across all targets. If the movement to the next target exceeds one hundred degrees on either axis, the telescope must perform a calibration step which adds ten extra degrees to the tracker. Return the total degrees moved as an integer.

title: Farming Crop Rotation
spec: Implement `farm(seasons)` to track soil health. The input is a list of strings representing the crop planted each season, such as corn, beans, or fallow. The field starts with a nitrogen level of fifty and a moisture level of fifty. Corn decreases nitrogen by twenty and moisture by ten, while beans increase nitrogen by ten but decrease moisture by fifteen. Fallow seasons increase both metrics by ten. If nitrogen drops below twenty, corn yields fail and the season is recorded as a loss. If moisture drops below ten, any planted crop fails. Return a tuple of the final nitrogen level, final moisture level, and the total count of failed seasons.

title: Sewing Pattern Scaler
spec: Write `scale(points, factor)` to adjust a garment pattern. The input is a list of tuples representing two dimensional coordinates of a clothing pattern, and a float scale factor. The program must first find the bounding box of all points to determine the exact center coordinates. Every point must then be moved outward or inward from the center by multiplying its distance to the center by the scale factor. If a scaled point falls into a negative coordinate space, shift the entire pattern so the minimum coordinate on both axes is exactly zero. Return the final adjusted list of coordinates rounded to the nearest integer.

title: Brewery Fermentation
spec: Create a function `monitor(readings)` to track a brew. The input is a list of tuples containing daily temperature and specific gravity measurements of a fermenting beverage. The process is complete when the specific gravity remains unchanged for three consecutive days. If the temperature exceeds twenty five degrees at any point, a warning flag is raised for off flavors. If the temperature drops below fifteen degrees, the fermentation stalls and needs a manual reset, which ignores the gravity reading for that specific day. Return a tuple containing the final specific gravity, the number of days it took to finish, and a boolean indicating if an off flavor warning was triggered.

title: Wind Turbine Output
spec: Implement `generate(speeds)` to calculate energy production. The input is a list of hourly wind speeds in meters per second. The turbine generates zero power if the wind is below three meters per second or above twenty five meters per second. Between three and twelve meters per second, power generation increases quadratically by squaring the wind speed and multiplying by ten. Between twelve and twenty five meters per second, it outputs a constant maximum of fourteen hundred and forty. Accumulate the total power generated over the period. Return a tuple containing the total energy produced and the number of hours the turbine was shut down due to high winds.

title: Cable Car Capacity
spec: Write `board(groups)` to load passengers onto a mountain lift. The input is a list of integers representing the number of people in waiting tourist groups. Each cable car cabin can hold a maximum of eight people. Groups must be boarded in the order they arrive, and a group cannot be split across multiple cabins. If a group cannot fit into the current cabin, the cabin is dispatched and a new one is loaded. If a single group is larger than eight people, they are denied boarding entirely and removed from the queue. Return the total number of cabins dispatched and the number of people who successfully boarded.

title: Archery Target Scorer
spec: Create `score(arrows)` to tally a competition. The input is a list of tuples representing the cartesian coordinates where arrows landed on a target. The target has five concentric rings with radii of two, four, six, eight, and ten. An arrow landing strictly inside or on the edge of a ring scores ten, eight, six, four, or two points respectively, from the center outward. If an arrow lands outside the radius of ten, it scores zero points. Count how many consecutive times an arrow scores zero. If three consecutive zeroes occur, the archer is disqualified and their total score is permanently reduced to zero. Return the final score integer.

title: Recycling Plant Sorter
spec: Implement `process(items)` to sort waste. The input is a list of tuples containing an item material string and its weight in kilograms. There are three processing bins for paper, plastic, and glass, each with a capacity of fifty kilograms. Iterate through the items and add their weight to the matching bin. If a bin exceeds its capacity, the excess weight is sent to a general landfill counter. Any item with a material not matching the three bins is considered contamination and immediately adds its entire weight to the landfill counter. Return a tuple containing the final weight in the landfill and the number of perfectly filled bins.

title: Pottery Kiln Controller
spec: Write a function `fire(temperatures)` to manage a ceramic firing schedule. The input is a list of target temperatures for sequential hours. The kiln starts at twenty degrees. It can heat up by a maximum of two hundred degrees per hour and cool down by a maximum of one hundred degrees per hour. If a target requires a larger jump or drop, the kiln uses its maximum rate instead and extends the schedule by inserting additional hours until the target is reached. Track the total hours the kiln operates. Return a tuple of the final completed temperature profile as a list of integers, and the total duration in hours.

title: Typing Speed Grader
spec: Create `evaluate(keystrokes, target)` to test a typist. The first parameter is a list of tuples containing a typed character and the time elapsed in seconds since the start. The second parameter is the exact target sentence string. Compare the typed characters to the target string sequentially. A character is an error if it does not match the corresponding character in the target string, and backspaces are not simulated. Calculate the final words per minute by dividing the total correct characters by five, then normalizing to a sixty second minute based on the final timestamp. Return the integer words per minute and the total error count.

title: Marathon Hydration Planner
spec: Implement `plan(stations)` to strategize a race. The input is a list of distances in kilometers where water stations are located along a route. A runner consumes two hundred milliliters of water for every kilometer run and carries a flask that holds five hundred milliliters. The runner starts with a full flask at kilometer zero. At each station, the runner refills the flask to maximum capacity only if it is currently below half full. If the flask runs dry before reaching the next station, the runner suffers a dehydration penalty of five minutes. Return the total volume of water consumed and the number of penalties incurred.

title: Lighthouse Signal Flash
spec: Write `translate(flashes)` to decode a visual signal. The input is a list of integers representing the duration in seconds of consecutive light flashes. A flash of one second is a dot, and a flash of three seconds is a dash. Any other flash duration represents a gap between letters. Translate the valid dots and dashes into standard alphabetic characters using a simplified mapping where a single dot is the letter E, a single dash is T, two dots is I, and two dashes is M. If a sequence does not match these four letters, append a question mark. Return the translated string formed by concatenating the valid letters and question marks.

title: Bridge Weight Toll
spec: Create a function `calculate(vehicles)` to collect bridge fees. The input is a list of tuples containing the number of axles and the total vehicle weight in tons. The base toll is five dollars per axle. If the vehicle weighs more than ten tons, an overweight surcharge of two dollars is added for every ton over ten. Commercial trucks, defined as having more than four axles, receive a ten percent discount on the total calculated toll. If the final toll includes a fraction, round it up to the next whole integer. Sum the tolls for all vehicles. Return a tuple containing the total revenue collected and the count of overweight vehicles.

title: Beehive Honey Tracker
spec: Implement `track(days)` to monitor a bee colony. The input is a list of tuples where the first element is the daily flower bloom index and the second is the weather condition string. The hive starts with ten units of honey. On sunny days, bees forage and add honey equal to the bloom index multiplied by two. On rainy days, bees stay inside and consume three units of honey. On cloudy days, they forage but only add the bloom index directly, consuming one unit. If honey drops to zero or below, the colony starves and the simulation halts. Return a tuple of the surviving days count and the final honey storage amount.

title: Parachute Deployment
spec: Write a function `descend(profile)` to simulate an object falling. The input is a list of wind resistance coefficients for descending altitude checkpoints. The object starts at ten thousand meters with a downward velocity of zero. At each checkpoint, gravity adds nine meters per second to the velocity, and air resistance subtracts the velocity multiplied by the coefficient. The parachute automatically deploys, multiplying all subsequent resistance coefficients by ten, when the altitude drops below three thousand meters or the velocity exceeds one hundred meters per second. Return a list of recorded velocities at each checkpoint rounded to the nearest integer.

title: Bicycle Gear Calculator
spec: Create `analyze(setup)` to evaluate a drivetrain. The input is a tuple containing a list of front chainring tooth counts and a list of rear cog tooth counts. The wheel circumference is fixed at two meters. For every possible combination of front and rear gears, calculate the gear ratio by dividing the front by the rear. Then calculate the development length, which is the gear ratio multiplied by the circumference. Discard any combinations where the chain is excessively crossed, defined as using the largest front ring with the largest rear cog, or the smallest of both. Return a list of valid development lengths sorted in ascending order.

title: Submarine Sonar Ping
spec: Implement `scan(echoes)` to process acoustic returns. The input is a list of echo return times in seconds. The speed of sound in water is fifteen hundred meters per second. Calculate the distance to each object by multiplying the return time by the speed of sound and dividing by two. If an object is closer than fifty meters, it triggers a proximity alert. If an object is between fifty and two hundred meters away, it is marked as tracking. Objects further than two hundred meters are ignored entirely. Return a tuple containing the number of proximity alerts and the maximum distance among the objects that are actively being tracked.

title: Vinyl Record Grooves
spec: Write `playback(scratches)` to assess audio degradation. The input is a list of integers representing the angular position of scratches on a vinyl record. The record spins at thirty three revolutions per minute. As a virtual stylus traverses three full rotations from angle zero to one thousand and eighty, it checks if its current angle modulo three hundred sixty matches a scratch location. Every match reduces the audio quality score, which starts at one hundred, by five points. If a scratch is located exactly at angle zero modulo three hundred sixty, it causes the stylus to skip forward by ten degrees. Return the final audio quality score and the total degrees traversed.

title: Sewing Machine Stitches
spec: Create `stitch(fabric, reinforced)` to measure thread durability. The first parameter is a list of strings representing layers of fabric, where thick reduces needle durability by three, medium by two, and thin by one. The needle starts with a durability of twenty. A stitch passes through all layers simultaneously, so the durability cost is the sum of the layer penalties. If the needle durability reaches zero or falls below it, the needle breaks and the remaining stitches fail. The reinforced boolean parameter doubles the durability cost but adds two to the final strength score. Return the total completed stitches and the final strength score.

title: Ski Jump Scoring
spec: Implement `judge(jumps)` to calculate competition results. The input is a list of tuples, each containing a jump distance in meters and a list of five style scores from different judges. The base points for a jump are sixty, plus two points for every meter beyond one hundred and twenty meters, or minus two points for every meter short. Sort the five style scores, discard the highest and lowest, and sum the remaining three. Add this style sum to the distance points to get the final jump score. If a jump score ends up negative, clamp it to zero. Return a list of the final scores rounded to one decimal place.

title: Paint Color Blender
spec: The function `blend(colors, multiplier)` takes a list of color tuples containing a pigment name string, a volume integer, and a unit string, along with a numeric multiplier.
