It scales the volume by the multiplier. If the scaled volume is greater than ten and the unit is drops, convert it to milliliters by dividing by ten and changing the unit string. If the unit is milliliters and the volume exceeds one thousand, convert it to liters by dividing by one thousand. Return the updated list of color tuples. For example, passing red, twenty, drops and a multiplier of two returns red, four, milliliters.

title: Terrarium Pet Compatibility
spec: The function `evaluate(reptiles, volume)` takes a list of tuples representing pets, each with a species string, an adult size integer in inches, and a temperament integer from one to ten, plus the terrarium volume integer in gallons. It calculates the sum of all sizes. If the total size exceeds the terrarium volume, the enclosure is overstocked. It also checks if any reptile has a temperament greater than seven while another has a size less than three inches, which indicates danger. Return a tuple containing a boolean for whether it is overstocked and a boolean for whether small pets are in danger.

title: Microscope Slide Analyzer
spec: The function `analyze(slides, threshold)` processes a list of tissue samples. It takes a list of slide tuples, each containing a sample identifier string, a cell count integer, and a clarity score float, plus a minimum clarity threshold float. It iterates through the slides, discarding any with a clarity score below the threshold. For the remaining slides, it calculates the average cell count. It then identifies all valid slides that have a cell count strictly greater than this average. Return a list of the sample identifiers for these high density slides.

title: Ferry Ticketing System
spec: The function `revenue(vehicles, passengers)` calculates the earnings for a boat trip. It receives a list of vehicle string types, which can be car, truck, or motorcycle, and a list of passenger counts for each vehicle. A car costs twenty dollars, a truck fifty dollars, and a motorcycle ten dollars. Each passenger adds an extra five dollars. If a truck has more than two passengers, a heavy load surcharge of fifteen dollars is applied to that vehicle. Return the total revenue collected from all vehicles.

title: Drawbridge Raise Timer
spec: The function `signal(boats, cars)` computes the optimal duration to keep a bridge raised. It takes a list of waiting boat sizes in meters and a list of waiting car counts. Each boat adds five seconds to the base raise time of twenty seconds, plus an extra ten seconds if the boat size exceeds fifty meters. Each waiting car reduces the raise time by two seconds to alleviate traffic, but the total time cannot drop below thirty seconds. Return the final calculated raise duration.

title: Hydroelectric Dam Output
spec: The function `yields(turbines, flow)` calculates total electricity production. It receives a list of turbine tuples with an identifier string, a capacity float, and an efficiency float, alongside a list of daily water flow floats. For each day and each turbine, the energy generated is the product of capacity, efficiency, and the day's water flow. If a turbine produces less than ten units of energy on any day, it is flagged as underperforming. Return a tuple containing the grand total of energy produced and a list of unique identifiers for underperforming turbines.

title: Mountain Trail Grader
spec: The function `grade(elevations)` evaluates a hiking route based on a list of altitude integers recorded at regular intervals. It calculates the total ascent by summing all positive elevation changes between consecutive points, and the total descent by summing all negative changes. It also finds the maximum steepness, which is the largest absolute difference between any two consecutive points. If the total ascent exceeds one thousand and the maximum steepness is over fifty, classify it as hard, otherwise easy. Return a tuple with the classification string, total ascent, and total descent.

title: Helicopter Payload Loader
spec: The function `load(crates, limit)` distributes supplies into transport flights. It takes a list of crate weight integers and a maximum weight limit integer per flight. It iterates through the crates and adds each to the current flight's payload. If adding a crate would exceed the limit, a new flight is started with that crate. If any single crate exceeds the flight limit, it is skipped entirely. Return a tuple containing the number of flights required and the sum of the weights of any skipped crates.

title: Vintage Coin Appraiser
spec: The function `value(coins, threshold)` calculates the total worth of a collection. It accepts a list of coin tuples, each holding a metal string, a mint year integer, a face value float, and a condition string, plus an age threshold integer. It sums the face values of all coins. If a coin's mint year is older than the threshold, its value is multiplied by five. If the condition string is mint, the value is doubled after the age multiplier. Return the final adjusted total value of the entire collection.

title: Banquet Seating Arranger
spec: The function `arrange(guests, capacity)` organizes a seating plan for a large dinner. It takes a list of guest group sizes and a table capacity integer. It iterates through the groups. If a group fits at the current table, they are added to it. If adding the group would exceed the capacity, the current table is finalized, and the group is seated at a new empty table. If any single group is larger than the table capacity, they are immediately placed in an overflow list and skipped. Return a tuple with the list of finalized table group counts and the number of guests in the overflow list.

title: Escalator Maintenance Tracker
spec: The function `maintenance(logs)` evaluates the usage of a mechanical staircase. It takes a list of daily usage integers representing the number of people who rode it. It maintains a running total of the cumulative usage. Whenever the cumulative usage exceeds ten thousand, a maintenance cycle is triggered and the running total is reset to zero. If any single day has a usage over two thousand, it triggers an emergency inspection. Return a tuple with the total number of maintenance cycles and the number of emergency inspections.

title: Server Room Thermal Monitor
spec: The function `control(readings, bounds)` manages a datacenter cooling system. It takes a list of temperature floats and a tuple containing the minimum and maximum acceptable temperatures. It iterates through the readings. If a reading is below the minimum, it records a heat action. If it is above the maximum, it records a cool action. If the temperature is within bounds, it records an idle action. However, if three consecutive cool actions occur, the fourth action must be a critical alert instead. Return a list of the recorded action strings.

title: Assembly Line Quality Control
spec: The function `inspect(items, tolerance)` evaluates manufactured parts. It receives a list of item tuples containing a length float, a width float, and a height float, and a tolerance percentage float. The ideal dimensions are ten, five, and two respectively. If any dimension of an item deviates from the ideal by more than the tolerance percentage, the item is defective. Otherwise, it is accepted. Return a tuple with the count of accepted items and the count of defective items.

title: Mine Shaft Elevator Tracker
spec: The function `track(commands, maximum)` monitors an underground lift. It accepts a list of command tuples containing a direction string which is either descend or ascend, and a distance integer, alongside a maximum safe depth integer. Starting at surface level zero, it updates the current depth based on the commands. If the current depth ever strictly exceeds the maximum safe depth, a cable warning flag is set. If an ascend command would bring the lift above zero, the depth is capped at zero. Return a tuple containing the final depth and the warning flag boolean.

title: Pipeline Inspection Robot
spec: The function `route(waypoints)` calculates the total travel distance for an autonomous crawler. It takes a list of waypoint tuples, each containing an x coordinate integer, a y coordinate integer, and a status string which is either clear or obstructed. The distance between consecutive waypoints is the sum of the absolute differences in their x and y coordinates. If the destination waypoint is obstructed, add a flat penalty of twenty distance units to account for navigation difficulty. Return the total calculated distance across all waypoints.

title: Meteorological Balloon Array
spec: The function `swarm(balloons, radius)` ensures a group of floating sensors remain in a tight formation. It receives a list of coordinate tuples containing x, y, and z floats, and a signal radius float. The first tuple in the list is the primary relay. For every other sensor, it calculates the straight line distance to the primary relay using the square root of the sum of squared coordinate differences. If this distance exceeds the radius, the sensor is considered disconnected. Return the count of disconnected sensors.

title: Grain Silo Inventory
spec: The function `levels(deposits, withdrawals)` simulates monthly agricultural storage. It takes two lists of floats representing monthly incoming and outgoing grain tonnages. The silo starts at five hundred tons and has a maximum capacity of two thousand tons. For each month, it adds the deposit and subtracts the withdrawal. If the tonnage exceeds two thousand, the excess is sold off, and the tonnage becomes two thousand. If the tonnage drops below zero, a deficit is recorded, and the tonnage becomes zero. Return a tuple containing the total sold tonnage and the total deficit tonnage.

title: Optical Prism Wavelengths
spec: The function `refract(angles)` determines the color bands produced by a glass structure. It takes a list of entry angle floats. For each angle, it calculates the wavelength by multiplying the sine of the angle by six hundred. If the wavelength is between four hundred and four hundred ninety, it maps to a blue band. If it is between four hundred ninety and five hundred seventy, it maps to a green band. Otherwise, it maps to a red band. Return a list of the resulting color band strings.

title: Ceramic Glaze Allocator
spec: The function `glaze(pots, supply)` distributes a liquid coating among clay vessels. It accepts a list of pot tuples containing a shape string and a quantity integer, plus a total supply integer. A bowl shape requires two units of supply per item, a plate requires three units, and a vase requires five. It processes pots in order. If the remaining supply is sufficient for a batch, it subtracts the required amount and adds the shape to a completed list. Otherwise, it skips the batch. Return the completed list and the remaining supply.

title: Cruise Ship Embarkation
spec: The function `board(passengers)` determines the order in which guests enter a luxury liner. It receives a list of passenger tuples containing a name string, a loyalty tier integer, and an accessibility needs boolean. It separates them into three lists. Anyone with accessibility needs goes into a special assistance list. From the remaining, those with a loyalty tier above five go into a VIP list, and the rest into a standard list. It sorts each list alphabetically by name. Return a single combined list of names starting with special assistance, then VIP, then standard.

title: Car Wash Queue Estimator
spec: The function `queue(arrivals, rate)` estimates the delay for an automated cleaning station. It takes a list of integer arrival times in minutes and an integer rate representing how many vehicles the station can wash per minute. It assumes one vehicle arrives at each given time. It calculates when each vehicle enters the wash, keeping track of the current available entry time. The wait time is the difference between entry time and arrival time. Return a list of wait times for all arrivals.

title: Knitting Machine Pattern Validator
spec: The function `analyze(stitches)` processes a list of mechanical operation strings. It scans through the sequence, counting occurrences of knit, purl, and drop. If it encounters three drop operations in a row without a knit or purl between them, it triggers a structural flaw flag. If a purl occurs as the very first operation, it records a boundary violation. Return a tuple containing the total drop count, the structural flaw boolean, and the boundary violation boolean.

title: Zoo Animal Dietary Planner
spec: The function `feed(animals)` determines daily nutrition requirements for an enclosure. It accepts a list of tuple records containing a species string, a weight float, and a pregnant boolean. If the species is lion, they need zero point eight units of meat per unit of weight. If the species is zebra, they need zero point four units of grass per unit of weight. If the species is monkey, they need zero point two units of fruit and zero point one units of insects per unit of weight. If any animal is pregnant, double their specific requirements. Return a tuple containing the total meat, grass, fruit, and insect amounts required.

title: Seismograph Tremor Peak Finder
spec: The function `align(vibrations)` finds the strongest localized shockwave in a geological reading. It takes a list of vibration amplitude floats measured at consecutive time intervals. It searches for a local maximum, which is an amplitude strictly greater than both the immediately preceding and immediately following values. The first and last values in the list cannot be local maxima. If multiple local maxima exist, it selects the one with the highest absolute amplitude. Return a tuple with the index of the strongest peak and its amplitude. If no local maximum is found, return negative one and zero point zero.

title: Vineyard Grape Harvest
spec: The function `harvest(vines, weather)` forecasts agricultural output for a winery. It takes a list of vine tuples containing a variety string and an age integer, plus a weather condition string. A merlot vine produces twenty units if its age is over four, otherwise zero. A chardonnay vine produces thirty units if its age is over six, otherwise ten. If the weather condition is frost, reduce the total yield of all vines by thirty percent. If it is sunny, increase the total yield by fifteen percent. Return the final predicted yield as a float.

title: Solar Eclipse Predictor
spec: Write a function `eclipse(orbits)` where the input is a list of lists representing celestial bodies, each containing an orbital radius, a speed, and an initial angle. The function must simulate three hundred and sixty days. On each day, update the angle of every body by adding its speed. Then check if any three bodies align by comparing their angles modulo three hundred and sixty. If the difference between the angles of three bodies is less than two degrees, count it as an alignment event. Return the total number of alignment events across the simulated period. Example: an input with bodies at radius ten speed two angle zero, radius twenty speed five angle ten, and radius thirty speed eight angle twenty might return five.

title: Skipping Rope Contest
spec: Implement `skip(jumps)` to score a jump rope routine where the input is a list of strings representing jump types like single, double, cross, or trip. The participant starts with one hundred stamina points. A single jump costs one stamina and scores one point, a double costs three stamina and scores four points, and a cross costs two stamina and scores three points. If a trip occurs, stamina drops by five and the current combo multiplier resets to one, otherwise the multiplier increases by one for every five consecutive successful jumps. If stamina falls to zero or below, the routine immediately ends. Return the final score. Example input containing ten single jumps and one trip returns a score of twelve.

title: Aqueduct Water Flow
spec: Create `flow(grid)` to trace water pressure through a roman aqueduct represented as a list of lists of characters. Water starts at the top left with a pressure of one hundred. An empty space drops pressure by one, a turn drops it by five, and a filter drops it by ten. If the water hits a blockage, it must attempt to route downwards or rightwards, prioritizing the direction with fewer adjacent blockages. If pressure reaches zero, the water stops flowing. Return a tuple containing the final row and column reached by the water and the remaining pressure. Example: a ten by ten grid with straight paths and one turn might output the bottom right corner coordinates and a pressure of eighty.

title: Constellation Mapper
spec: Write `constellations(stars)` to group stars into constellations. The input is a list of tuples containing the horizontal and vertical coordinates of stars. Compare every pair of stars; if their geometric distance is less than or equal to fifteen units, they belong to the same constellation group. Iterate through all stars and merge groups when a star bridges two separate clusters. Discard any group that contains fewer than four stars, as they are too small to be a constellation. Return the number of valid constellation groups. Example: passing ten stars where five are tightly clustered and five are spread far apart returns one.

title: Juggling Pattern Validator
spec: Implement `juggle(sequence)` to validate a juggling sequence given as a list of integer throw heights. Maintain a schedule of landing times for each ball. For each throw in the sequence, add the throw height to the current beat index to determine when the ball will land. If two balls are scheduled to land on the exact same beat, a collision occurs and the pattern is invalid. Also check that the average of all throw heights equals a whole number, which represents the number of balls required. Return a tuple with a boolean indicating if the pattern is valid and the number of balls used. Example: a sequence of three, four, five returns valid and four balls.

title: Trampoline Park Bouncer
spec: Develop `bounce(trampolines)` where the input is a list of integers representing the bounce strength of trampolines in a line. A jumper starts at the first trampoline. At each step, they bounce forward a number of spaces equal to the strength of the trampoline they are currently on. If they land on a trampoline with an even strength, their next bounce distance is halved, rounded down. If they land on a prime strength, their next bounce is doubled. The routine ends when the jumper bounces past the end of the list or gets stuck on a trampoline with zero strength. Return the number of jumps made. Example: a sequence of two, three, one, four might result in four jumps.

title: Clock Pendulum Calibrator
spec: Write `calibrate(readings)` to adjust a grandfather clock based on environmental data. The input is a list of tuples containing temperature and humidity percentages over several days. The ideal pendulum length is exactly one meter. For every degree above twenty degrees, the pendulum expands by one millimeter, slowing the clock by two seconds per day. For every ten percent humidity above fifty, the wood swells, slowing the clock by an additional second. Calculate the total lost or gained seconds for each day and sum them up. Return the total time drift in seconds. Example: five days at twenty five degrees and sixty humidity returns a drift of fifty five seconds.

title: Fossil Layer Excavator
spec: Implement `excavate(site)` to process an archaeological dig site provided as a list of lists of strings representing soil types and bone fragments. You must dig layer by layer from top to bottom. If you encounter solid rock, you cannot dig any deeper in that specific vertical column. When you find a bone fragment, check its surrounding cells in all eight directions; if adjacent to ash, the bone is deemed ancient, but if adjacent to mud, it is considered recent. Count the number of ancient and recent bones found before hitting rock in all columns. Return a list containing the ancient count and the recent count. Example: a grid with three bones near ash and one near mud returns three and one.

title: Radio Telescope Array
spec: Create `scan(signals)` to process data from multiple radio dishes. The input is a list of lists of numbers representing radio frequencies received by each dish over time. To find a true astronomical event, a frequency spike greater than fifty must occur on at least three different dishes at the exact same time index. However, if a spike occurs on all dishes simultaneously, it is considered earth interference and must be ignored. Count the number of valid astronomical events and also find the highest frequency recorded during those specific events. Return a tuple of the event count and the maximum valid frequency. Example: a list of four dishes over ten time steps might yield two events and a max frequency of eighty.

title: Origami Fold Simulator
spec: Write `fold(instructions)` to simulate folding a square piece of paper originally ten units by ten units with a thickness of one. The input is a list of strings detailing the fold directions, such as horizontal, vertical, or diagonal. A horizontal fold halves the width and doubles the thickness. A vertical fold halves the height and doubles the thickness. A diagonal fold divides the area by two, changes the shape, and doubles the thickness, but a diagonal fold cannot be performed if the current thickness is greater than eight. If an invalid fold is attempted, skip it. Return a tuple containing the final thickness and the final visible area. Example: a horizontal fold followed by a vertical fold yields a thickness of four and an area of twenty five.

title: Kite Flying Contest
spec: Develop `kite(winds)` to track the altitude of a kite. The input is a list of wind speeds measured every minute. The kite starts at zero altitude. If the wind speed is between ten and twenty, the altitude increases by five units. If the wind is above twenty, the altitude decreases by two units due to instability, unless the kite is already above fifty units, in which case it holds steady. If the wind drops below ten, the kite falls by ten units. The altitude can never go below zero. Return the maximum altitude reached during the flight and the final altitude at the end of the data. Example: ten minutes of ideal wind might return fifty and fifty.

title: Sandcastle Tide Defense
spec: Implement `tide(walls)` to determine how long a sandcastle survives incoming waves. The input is a list of integers representing the heights of circular defensive walls from outermost to innermost. The tide starts at height zero and increases by one every hour. Each hour, a wave hits the outermost remaining wall. If the wave height exceeds the wall height, that wall washes away, and the next wave will hit the next inner wall. If the tide exceeds the innermost wall, the castle falls. Return the number of hours the castle survives. Example: walls of height two, four, and five will survive for six hours.

title: Meteor Shower Spotter
spec: Write `meteors(conditions)` to calculate visible meteors. The input is a list of tuples containing cloud cover percentage, moon brightness percentage, and base meteor rate per hour. For each hour, start with the base rate. Reduce the rate by the cloud cover percentage. Then, subtract half of the moon brightness percentage from the remaining rate. If the resulting visible rate drops below zero, record it as zero. Sum the visible meteors across all hours and return the integer total, rounding down any fractions. Example: three hours with zero clouds and fifty percent moon brightness on a base rate of twenty returns thirty.

title: Hot Air Balloon Navigator
spec: Create `navigate(layers)` to steer a balloon towards a target. The input is a list of tuples representing atmospheric layers, each providing a wind direction in degrees and a speed. The balloon starts at the first layer and a horizontal position of zero. It needs to travel exactly one hundred units forward. Each minute, the balloon moves according to the current layer's speed. To minimize sideways drift, check the wind directions; if the current layer causes a drift greater than ten degrees from straight ahead, the balloon must ascend to the next layer for the next minute. Return the total sideways drift accumulated when the forward goal is reached. Example: traveling through three layers with minor drift might return a total drift of fifteen.

title: Coral Reef Bleaching
spec: Implement `coral(temperatures)` to simulate reef health over a summer. The input is a list of daily ocean temperatures. The reef starts with one hundred health points. If the temperature exceeds thirty degrees for three consecutive days, a bleaching event begins, causing the reef to lose five health points each subsequent day the temperature remains above twenty eight degrees. If the temperature drops below twenty five degrees, the reef recovers two points per day up to its maximum of one hundred. Return the final health of the reef and the number of days it spent in a bleaching state. Example: a twenty day heatwave might return fifty health and fifteen bleaching days.

title: Glacier Melting Tracker
spec: Write `glacier(climate)` to model the mass of a glacier. The input is a list of tuples, each containing a season name and the average temperature. The glacier begins with a mass of ten thousand units. During winter, if the temperature is below zero, it gains fifty units of mass. During summer, it loses ten units of mass for every degree above zero. Spring and autumn have no direct melting unless the previous season was a summer warmer than twenty degrees, which causes a residual loss of twenty units. If the mass ever reaches zero, it cannot recover. Return the final mass. Example: alternating cold winters and mild summers over ten years might result in a mass of ten thousand two hundred.

title: Tornado Siren Network
spec: Develop `sirens(grid)` to determine siren activation in a county. The input is a list of lists of characters representing a map where towns are marked and sirens are marked. A tornado touches down at the top left corner and moves diagonally to the bottom right. As it moves, any siren within three grid units of the tornado's current position activates. An active siren alerts all towns within a five unit radius. Count how many unique towns receive an alert before the tornado leaves the grid. Return this count. Example: a ten by ten grid with two sirens and three towns might return all three towns alerted.

title: Subway Train Delays
spec: Implement `subway(schedule)` to calculate cascading delays on a transit line. The input is a list of tuples containing a train identifier, a scheduled arrival time in minutes, and an actual arrival time. Sort the schedule by the scheduled time. If a train arrives more than five minutes late, it causes congestion. The next train scheduled to arrive after a congested train will be delayed by half the delay time of the previous train, rounded down, in addition to its own delay. Sum the final delay times of all trains after congestion adjustments. Return the total network delay. Example: five trains where the first is twenty minutes late might cause a total delay of thirty eight minutes.

title: Avalanche Risk Assessor
spec: Write `avalanche(slopes)` to evaluate mountain safety. The input is a list of tuples representing different mountain faces, each with a steepness angle, a recent snowfall amount, and a temperature shift. A slope is considered dangerous if the angle is between thirty and forty five degrees and the recent snowfall exceeds twenty units. However, if the temperature shift is positive and greater than five degrees, the snow settles and the snowfall threshold for danger increases to thirty units. Count the number of slopes categorized as dangerous and the number deemed safe. Return a list with the dangerous count followed by the safe count. Example: four slopes with varying angles and high snow might return two dangerous and two safe.

title: Bat Cave Echo Location
spec: Create `echo(bounces)` to map a cave based on sound waves. The input is a list of return times in milliseconds for echolocation pings sent in various directions. Sound travels at three hundred and forty meters per second. Calculate the distance for each ping by halving the time and multiplying by the speed. If a distance is less than two meters, flag it as an immediate obstacle. If a sequence of three consecutive pings in the list indicates an immediate obstacle, the bat must turn around, abandoning the rest of the data. Return the number of obstacles detected before a turn around occurs. Example: ten pings with early short returns might return three obstacles.

title: Pigeon Homing Race
spec: Develop `pigeons(checkpoints)` to simulate a bird's race home. The input is a list of tuples detailing the distance to the next checkpoint and the weather condition, like clear, rainy, or windy. The pigeon flies at sixty kilometers per hour in clear weather, forty in rain, and fifty in windy conditions. The bird must rest for twelve hours if it accumulates more than ten hours of continuous flight. Calculate the total time in hours, including rest periods, it takes the pigeon to pass all checkpoints. Return the total time rounded to the nearest whole hour. Example: three checkpoints of five hundred kilometers in clear weather might take thirty seven hours.

title: Lumberjack Tree Felling
spec: Implement `lumber(forest)` to simulate harvesting timber. The input is a list of lists of integers representing tree heights in a grid. A harvester starts at the bottom left and attempts to fell trees larger than twenty units. When a tree is cut, it falls to the right. If its height is greater than the distance to the next tree in that row, it damages that adjacent tree, reducing its height by five units. Traverse the grid row by row from bottom to top, felling all eligible trees and applying damage. Return the total number of trees successfully harvested. Example: a small grid with dense, tall trees might yield a harvest of ten.

title: Billiard Ball Collision
spec: Write `billiards(shots)` to track balls on a pool table. The input is a list of tuples containing initial horizontal and vertical velocities for a cue ball. The table is one hundred units wide and two hundred units long. For each shot, simulate the ball's path until its velocity drops to zero, decreasing both velocity components by one unit per time step due to friction. If the ball hits a table edge, its velocity in that perpendicular direction reverses. Count how many times the ball bounces off any cushion before stopping. Return the total number of bounces across all shots. Example: three strong shots might result in a total of twelve bounces.

title: Scuba Diver Decompression
spec: Create `scuba(profile)` to calculate safety stops for a diver. The input is a list of tuples containing a depth in meters and a time spent at that depth in minutes. Calculate the total nitrogen load by multiplying depth by time for each segment and adding it to a running total. When ascending, if the total load exceeds five hundred, the diver must stop at five meters for three minutes, which reduces the load by two hundred. If the load still exceeds five hundred after the stop, they must wait another three minutes. Return the total number of minutes spent at the safety stop. Example: a deep, long dive might require nine minutes of stops.

title: Fireworks Display Sequencer
spec: Develop `fireworks(shells)` to organize a pyrotechnic show. The input is a list of tuples containing a launch time, a fuse length, and a color. Calculate the exact explosion time for each shell by adding the fuse length to the launch time. Sort the explosions chronologically. To ensure a good show, check for dark skies; if the gap between any two consecutive explosions is greater than ten seconds, add a warning penalty of one to a counter. If three red shells explode in a row, add a bonus point to the show score. Return a tuple of the total warning penalties and the total bonus points. Example: a well-timed list of twenty shells with clustered reds might return zero penalties and two bonuses.

title: Planet Orbit Resonance Validator
spec: The function `resonate(planets, threshold)` analyzes planetary orbital periods to find gravitational resonances. The first parameter is a list of tuples containing the planet name, its orbital period in days, and its mass. The function compares every unique pair of planets to determine the ratio of their periods by dividing the larger by the smaller. It checks if this ratio falls within the given threshold of exact fractions specifically three halves, two thirds, or four thirds, adding their combined mass to a stability score if they match, while highly resonant pairs near exactly two or three add triple their combined mass. Should any single planet participate in three or more resonance pairs, the system is chaotic and returns negative one, otherwise it returns the stability score rounded down. Example input earth three hundred sixty five mass one and mars six hundred eighty seven mass zero point one with threshold zero point zero five returns four.

title: Geode Crystal Layer Analyzer
spec: The function `analyze(layers, depth)` determines the commercial value of a sliced geode based on its mineral bands. The inputs are a list of string colors representing concentric crystal layers from the outside in, and a numeric depth limit for processing. Iterating up to the depth, a purple layer adds fifty to the base value and a blue layer adds thirty, while a white layer immediately following a purple layer adds a rare contrast bonus of twenty. If consecutive brown layers are found the geode is muddy and the total value is halved, but if a green layer appears within the first three layers the geode is contaminated and returns zero. The function tracks distinct colors seen, applying a one point five multiplier to the final value if more than four distinct colors are found before the depth limit. For instance an input of brown, brown, purple, white with depth four returns forty five.

title: Sailboat Regatta Handicap Calculator
spec: The function `handicap(boats, wind)` adjusts race times for different classes of sailboats under specific weather conditions. The first parameter is a list of tuples containing the boat class name, its base completion time in minutes, and its hull length. If the wind is above twenty knots, boats under twenty five feet receive a ten percent time penalty due to waves while boats over forty feet get a five percent reduction. If the wind is below eight knots, all boats receive a flat fifteen minute penalty, except lighter boats under thirty feet which only receive five minutes. Any boat with an adjusted time over three hundred minutes is disqualified, and the function must return a list of remaining boat class names sorted from lowest to highest adjusted time. Example laser base sixty length fourteen and cruiser base fifty length thirty five at wind twenty five returns laser then cruiser.

title: Medieval Castle Siege Defender
spec: The function `defend(walls, attackers)` simulates a medieval castle holding off a siege over multiple days. The walls parameter lists the integer structural integrity of different wall sections, while attackers lists the damage dealt by the enemy on successive days. Each day the damage is distributed evenly across all intact wall sections, with any fractional remainder applied entirely to the section with the lowest current integrity. When a section drops to zero it is breached, and any future damage it would have taken is instead doubled and applied to adjacent walls. If more than half the original walls breach the castle falls and returns the number of days it lasted, otherwise it returns the sum of remaining integrity across all intact walls. Example walls hundred, hundred and attackers fifty, fifty returns one hundred fifty.

title: Perfume Scent Note Blender
spec: The function `blend(ingredients, volume)` calculates the final fragrance profile of a mixed perfume. The ingredients list contains tuples of a scent family string, a volatility rating from one to ten, and the added volume in milliliters. Ingredients with volatility eight or higher are top notes, four to seven are heart notes, and three or below are base notes. The longevity score starts at one hundred, but if top notes exceed fifty percent of the target total volume it drops by twenty percent, and if base notes are less than ten percent it is halved. A harmony bonus of fifteen is added if floral and woody families are both present, but mixing citrus directly with dairy returns zero. It returns the final longevity score capped at one hundred.

title: Magic Gathering Card Synergies
spec: The function `synergize(deck, rules)` evaluates a collection of fantasy playing cards to calculate a total synergy power rating. The deck parameter holds tuples of the card name, primary elemental type, and base power, while rules contains pairs of elements that combo together. Iterating over every unique pair of cards in the deck, if their elements match a rule combination their combined power is multiplied by one point five and added to a synergy tracker. Cards with the exact same elemental type but different names grant a flat bonus of five, while cards with the exact same name conflict and subtract ten. If the deck contains more than five distinct elemental types the overall tracker is reduced by twenty five percent, returning the final integer rating. Example deck fire goblin two and water sprite three with rules fire and water yields seven.

title: Teapot Heat Retention Modeler
spec: The function `model(materials, time)` estimates the temperature drop of water in various teapots over a given duration. The materials list provides the teapot material name, its thickness in millimeters, and its thermal conductivity coefficient. Starting at one hundred degrees celsius, each teapot loses temperature per minute equal to its conductivity coefficient divided by its thickness. Glass teapots lose an additional zero point five degrees per minute due to radiation, while cast iron retains a minimum temperature of sixty degrees regardless of elapsed time. Teapots falling below forty degrees are considered cold and no longer tracked. The function returns a list of tuples with the material and its final temperature rounded to one decimal place, sorted by highest remaining temperature.

title: Black Hole Event Horizon Proximity
spec: The function `calculate(masses, distances)` determines which observer spaceships can safely escape a gravitational pull. Masses is a list of numeric black hole masses, and distances is a list of lists containing spaceship names and their current distance from the corresponding black hole. The Schwarzschild radius for each black hole is its mass multiplied by two point nine five. Ships whose distance is less than or equal to the radius are spaghettified and added to a lost tally, while those within one and a half times the radius burn emergency fuel and append their names to a critical warning list. If a black hole over one thousand mass claims more than two ships the region is quarantined and returns a string indicating collapse, otherwise the function returns the critical warning list sorted alphabetically.

title: Snowplow Route Optimizer
spec: The function `plow(streets, snow)` calculates the total time required to clear a neighborhood after a winter storm. Streets is a list of tuples detailing the street name, length in kilometers, and priority level from one to three. Priority one streets are processed first, then priority two, and finally priority three, with base clearing time equal to length multiplied by snow depth divided by five. Priority one streets get ten extra minutes for salt if snow exceeds ten inches, while priority three streets are skipped if snow is under two inches. If priority one streets take more than one hundred twenty minutes, priority two clearing times increase by fifty percent due to vehicle fatigue. The function returns the total clearing time in minutes rounded to the nearest integer.

title: Honeycomb Structure Integrity
spec: The function `inspect(cells, pressure)` evaluates the resilience of a honeycomb section under external stress. The cells parameter contains tuples of the hexagonal row coordinate, column coordinate, and wax thickness in millimeters. Each cell starts with a base strength equal to its thickness multiplied by the pressure factor, gaining a ten percent bonus for every adjacent neighbor with a thickness greater than one millimeter. Cells with fewer than three neighbors are edge cells and suffer a fifteen percent strength penalty. If any cell drops below a final strength of two it ruptures, cascading a damage penalty of zero point five to all immediate neighbors which may cause further ruptures. The function tallies and returns the total number of ruptured cells.

title: Antique Clock Gear Ratios
spec: The function `ratio(gears, target)` finds the optimal sequence of cogwheels to achieve a specific rotational speed multiplier. The gears parameter lists the integer teeth counts on available cogwheels. The function must select exactly three distinct gears to act as driver, idler, and driven in order, ensuring the idler has at least half the teeth of the driver to prevent skipping. The mechanical advantage is the driven teeth divided by the driver teeth, and if this matches the target multiplier exactly it receives a friction score based on total teeth plus a five point penalty if the driven gear has an odd number of teeth. It returns a tuple of the three gear teeth counts that achieves the target ratio with the lowest possible friction score, or an empty tuple if impossible.

title: Butterfly Migration Thermal Drafts
spec: The function `migrate(drafts, energy)` tracks a swarm of monarch butterflies navigating upward wind currents. The drafts list represents altitude gain or loss provided by successive air currents, and energy is the starting stamina. Positive drafts lift the swarm by that amount and cost one energy, while negative drafts drop them unless they spend three energy to resist, which they will only do if the drop exceeds ten meters and they have at least five energy. If altitude ever drops below zero they land permanently and the function returns the draft index, and if energy hits exactly zero they must rest and skip the next two drafts entirely. The function returns their final altitude after processing all drafts.

title: Cuckoo Clock Chime Synchronizer
spec: The function `synchronize(clocks, minutes)` adjusts a collection of mechanical birds to chirp in unison over time. Clocks contains tuples of the bird name, chime interval in seconds, and current delay offset. Simulating time second by second up to the given minutes limit, a clock chimes if the current time minus its offset is a multiple of its interval. If multiple clocks chime at the exact same second their future offsets are permanently reduced by one second, but a clock chiming alone for three consecutive intervals falls out of sync and increases its offset by two seconds. The function returns the total count of chimes across all clocks during the simulation. Example clocks alpha interval ten offset zero and beta interval ten offset zero for one minute returns twelve.

title: Soap Bubble Surface Tension
spec: The function `tension(bubbles, humidity)` calculates the lifespan of floating suds before they pop. Bubbles contains tuples of the radius in centimeters, soap concentration percentage, and starting altitude, while humidity is a general moisture index. Base lifespan in seconds is concentration multiplied by radius, but humidity below forty reduces this by twenty percent and a radius over ten loses an additional five seconds. Bubbles drift downward at two meters per second, and if their starting altitude divided by descent rate is less than their lifespan they hit the ground and pop prematurely. The function filters out bubbles that hit the ground and returns the average natural lifespan of the surviving bubbles rounded to one decimal place.

title: Magic Wand Core Resonance
spec: The function `craft(cores, wood)` evaluates the compatibility of mystical crafting materials. Cores is a list of magical substance strings, and wood is the single string wand body material. When matched with mahogany wood, dragon cores gain fifty power but unicorn hairs lose twenty, while willow wood doubles the base one hundred power of any core containing the word feather. Cores longer than ten characters suffer a ten point stability penalty, and duplicate core materials only contribute half their calculated power to the overall total. If the final combined power of all cores exceeds five hundred the wand shatters and returns zero, otherwise it returns the total combined power.

title: Pirate Treasure Map Triangulation
spec: The function `triangulate(landmarks, clues)` processes geographical references to pinpoint a buried chest. Landmarks is a list of tuples containing a name, x coordinate, and y coordinate, while clues provides a starting landmark name, a compass direction string, and a distance in paces. Starting a dig site at zero zero, the function processes each clue by finding the matching landmark and moving the specified distance in the given direction, adding to y for north and x for east. Diagonal directions add to both axes but reduce the distance by twenty percent due to terrain. If the final dig site falls within ten paces of any known landmark it returns the string compromised, otherwise it returns the final rounded coordinates as a tuple.

title: Fencing Bout Point Assessor
spec: The function `score(touches, priority)` determines the winner of a swordplay match based on right of way rules. Touches is a list of exchanges containing the first fencer, second fencer, and time difference in milliseconds, while priority is the fencer currently holding right of way. If the time difference is over forty milliseconds it is a single touch and the first fencer scores a point, but forty or less is a double touch where the priority fencer scores and priority immediately swaps. If one fencer scores three unanswered points in a row they gain a one point momentum bonus. The bout ends immediately if a fencer reaches fifteen points, and the function returns the final scores for fencer a and fencer b as a tuple.

title: Hot Spring Mineral Composition
spec: The function `compose(minerals, temperature)` assesses the healing properties of a geothermal bath. Minerals is a list of tuples holding the mineral name, concentration, and solubility threshold. If a mineral's concentration exceeds its threshold at the given temperature, the excess precipitates out, reducing the concentration and subtracting five points from the score for cloudiness. Sulfur concentrations are doubled for the score if the temperature is above forty degrees, but hard water formed by calcium and magnesium both exceeding fifty reduces the overall score by twenty percent. Temperatures over fifty degrees halve all final mineral scores due to scalding heat, and the function returns the final therapeutic score rounded to the nearest whole number.

title: Tapestry Weaving Thread Count
spec: The function `weave(threads, pattern)` calculates the total yarn needed to produce a decorative wall hanging. Threads contains tuples of color name, thickness in millimeters, and elasticity percentage, while pattern lists the sequence of colors for each row. Each row has a base length requirement of one hundred centimeters, reduced by five if the thread elasticity is above ten percent. Gold and silver threads require special knotting that adds twenty centimeters per row, and if a requested color is missing from the threads list the first available substitute is used with a thirty centimeter splicing penalty. The function sums the adjusted lengths for all rows and returns the total required yarn in meters.

title: Ghost Hunting EMF Detector
spec: The function `detect(readings, baseline)` identifies paranormal activity from electromagnetic fluctuations. Readings contains milligauss floats recorded over time against a standard background baseline. A reading at least two and a half times the baseline is a spike, and three consecutive spikes form a manifestation event that adds fifty points to an activity tracker. Readings dropping below half the baseline are cold spots that add ten points, but a wild fluctuation directly from a spike to a cold spot resets the tracker to zero for that segment due to suspected malfunction. The function returns a tuple containing the final activity score and the total count of distinct manifestation events.

title: Bonsai Tree Pruning Simulator
spec: The function `prune(branches, season)` determines the optimal cuts to shape a miniature tree. Branches lists tuples of the branch identification number, length in centimeters, and current leaf count. In winter, branches over fifteen centimeters are cut back by a third and lose all leaves, while in spring branches with fewer than five leaves are removed entirely and drop to length zero. During summer branches with over twenty leaves have their leaf count halved to improve airflow but retain their length. If the total length of wood removed across all branches exceeds fifty centimeters the tree goes into shock and all remaining leaves drop to zero. The function returns a list of updated branch lengths and leaf counts.

title: Kite Surfing Wind Aerodynamics
spec: The function `surf(winds, board)` calculates the maximum jump height achieved by a rider over a series of waves. Winds is a list of wind gust speeds in knots, and board contains the weight in kilograms and kite area in square meters. Base lift is the gust speed multiplied by kite area minus the board weight, capping at fifty units if the wind exceeds thirty knots due to kite deformation. Three consecutive successful jumps with a height over ten build momentum and add a five unit bonus to the next jump. If a gust is exactly zero the rider falls and must spend the next two waves relaunching, scoring zero for them regardless of wind speed. The function returns the highest single jump height achieved.

title: Vaudeville Act Stage Timing
spec: The function `schedule(acts, breaks)` calculates the total duration of an old-fashioned variety show. Acts lists tuples of the performer name, routine duration in minutes, and prop setup time, while breaks is the standard intermission length. Performers who juggle require a specialized net that adds five minutes to their setup time, and any act exceeding twenty minutes triggers an impromptu break equal to half the standard intermission immediately following their routine. If three acts in a row require zero setup time the crew works ahead and reduces the fourth act's setup by three minutes. If cumulative show time surpasses one hundred twenty minutes all remaining acts have their duration cut by ten percent, returning the final total duration rounded up.

title: Truffle Pig Snout Proximity
spec: The function `forage(scents, area)` maps the path of a foraging animal through a woodland grid. Scents is a list of tuples containing the x coordinate, y coordinate, and pungency score of a buried fungus, while area defines the grid bounds. Starting at zero zero for up to twenty steps, the pig checks all scents within a three unit radius to find the highest pungency score. If there is a tie for highest the pig wanders one step northeast, otherwise it moves one unit along both axes toward the highest scent, digging it up and adding its pungency to a total yield once reached. Hitting the area boundaries bounces the pig back one step, and the function returns the total yield collected.

title: Slingshot Trajectory Calibrator
spec: The function `calibrate(bands, projectiles)` determines the optimal pairing of elastic and ammo for maximum distance. Bands contains tuples of material, elasticity multiplier, and maximum draw weight, while projectiles lists the ammo type, weight in grams, and drag coefficient. Initial velocity is draw weight multiplied by elasticity and divided by projectile weight, and distance is velocity squared divided by drag. A projectile weighing more than half the maximum draw weight snaps the band for zero distance, while lead projectiles ignore ten percent of their drag penalty. Bands achieving a distance over one thousand suffer microtears, permanently reducing their elasticity multiplier by zero point one for subsequent evaluations. The function returns the names of the optimal band and projectile pairing.

title: Typewriter Margin Bell Ringer
spec: Simulate a mechanical typewriter carriage returning a list of line lengths and a count of how many times the margin bell rings. Write the function typewrite(words) where the input is a list of integers representing the lengths of words being typed. The carriage has a maximum width of eighty characters. Every word advances the carriage by its length. A single space automatically separates words on the same line, consuming one unit of width. If adding the next word and the preceding space exceeds the remaining width, the carriage drops to a new line and the bell rings. The new line starts immediately with the word that did not fit. Return a tuple containing a list of the final line lengths in characters and the total number of bell rings. For example, given word lengths of forty, thirty, and twenty, it returns a list of two lengths and one bell ring.

title: Steampunk Valve Cascade
spec: Model a network of steam pipes that relieves pressure through cascading safety valves. Create the function vent(pressures) where the input is a list of integers representing initial steam pressure in consecutive pipe segments. When a segment exceeds fifty units of pressure, it vents exactly half of its total pressure, rounded down, to the next segment in the sequence. This venting is checked and resolved from the first segment to the last in a single pass. If the final segment exceeds fifty units, its vented pressure escapes into the atmosphere and is lost. Return a list of the final pressure values in all segments after one full left to right cascade. For example, given pressures of sixty, ten, and zero, it returns thirty, twenty five, and zero.

title: Jukebox Queue Manager
spec: Manage the mechanical queue of a vintage vinyl jukebox. Implement the function play(requests) where the input is a list of integer track identifiers. The jukebox can hold a maximum of five tracks in its active queue. If a request arrives and the queue is not full, it is added to the end. If the queue is full, incoming requests are ignored unless they are a duplicate of the currently playing track, which immediately ejects the active track and starts playing the next in the queue. A zero in the input list means the current track finishes naturally and the next one begins. Return a list of track identifiers in the exact order they finish playing. For example, given requests of one, two, zero, three, zero, it returns one and two.

title: Carousel Horse Oscillation
spec: Calculate the vertical positions of horses on a merry go round. Define the function carousel(rotations) taking an integer representing the number of complete machine rotations. The ride has four horses arranged in a circle, all starting at the bottom position of zero. A rotation is divided into four quarters. During each quarter rotation, the first and third horses move up by two units if they are at the bottom, or down by two units if they are at the top. The second and fourth horses do the exact opposite, moving down if they are at the top, or up if they are at the bottom. The maximum height is two units and the minimum is zero. Return a list of four integers representing the final vertical positions of the four horses. For example, given two rotations, it returns zero, zero, zero, and zero.

title: Mechanical Loom Weaver
spec: Simulate a manual weaving loom creating a fabric pattern. Write the function weave(threads) where the input is a list of integers representing colored thread spool numbers. The loom operates by passing a shuttle left to right, then right to left. On a left to right pass, odd numbered threads are placed on top of the fabric. On a right to left pass, even numbered threads are placed on top. If a zero is encountered in the list, the shuttle direction reverses immediately without placing any thread. Any thread that does not match the active direction rule is hidden underneath and not recorded. Return a list of the thread numbers that were placed on top of the fabric in their original order. For example, given threads of three, four, zero, five, it returns three and five.

title: Astrolabe Star Altitude
spec: Determine navigational latitude by measuring star elevations with an antique brass astrolabe. Create the function navigate(angles) where the input is a list of measured angles in degrees. To calibrate the instrument, the navigator takes the first three positive angles, discards the highest and lowest, and keeps the median. This median calibration value is then subtracted from all subsequent angles in the list, completely ignoring the first three used for calibration. Any resulting angle that falls below zero is considered a reading error and is discarded. Angles above ninety are capped at exactly ninety. Return a list of the final adjusted and valid angles. For example, given angles of ten, twenty, thirty, and forty, the calibration is twenty, so it returns twenty for the last angle.

title: Film Projector Reel Changeover
spec: Detect manual changeover cues on a dual reel cinema projector. Implement the function project(frames) where the input is a list of integers representing frame types. Standard frames are represented by ones and cue marks are represented by nines. A valid changeover sequence requires exactly two cue marks separated by at least ten standard frames but no more than twenty standard frames. If a valid sequence is detected, the projection successfully switches to the second reel and all subsequent frames in the input are ignored. Return the total number of frames projected before the successful changeover is complete, or the total length of the input if no valid changeover ever occurs. For example, given frames of one, nine, twelve ones, and nine, it returns fifteen.

title: Barometer Pressure Trend
spec: Predict weather patterns based on an antique mercury barometer. Define the function forecast(readings) taking a list of atmospheric pressure readings taken every hour. A rising trend is defined as three consecutive readings that increase by at least two units each time. A falling trend is defined as three consecutive readings that decrease by at least two units each time. If a rising trend is immediately followed by a falling trend within five hours, a storm is predicted. Return one if a storm is predicted, two for a simple rising trend, three for a simple falling trend, and zero for no significant pattern. For example, given readings of ten, twelve, and fourteen, it returns two.

title: Gramophone Stylus Wear
spec: Track the degradation of a diamond gramophone needle over time. Write the function stylus(records) where the input is a list of integers representing the lengths of audio tracks in minutes. A brand new needle starts with a sharpness score of one thousand. Each minute of normal playback reduces the sharpness by two points. If a track is longer than ten minutes, friction heats up the needle, causing every minute after the tenth to reduce the sharpness by five points instead of two. If the sharpness drops to zero or below, the needle shatters and all remaining tracks in the list are unplayable. Return a tuple containing the final sharpness score and the total number of unplayed tracks. For example, given records of five, fifteen, and twenty, it returns nine hundred fifteen and zero.

title: Quilt Patchwork Symmetry
spec: Evaluate if a quilter is sewing a symmetric blanket out of square fabric blocks. Create the function patchwork(blocks) where the input is a list of lists of integers, representing rows of fabric block styles. A row is considered perfectly symmetric if reading its elements left to right is identical to reading them right to left. The quilt is only valid if strictly more than half of its rows are perfectly symmetric. Additionally, the very first row and the very last row must be identical to each other. Return the integer one if the quilt design is valid, or zero if it fails any of these structural requirements. For example, a patchwork of three identical symmetric rows returns one.

title: Yoyo String Tension
spec: Simulate the twisting tension on a cotton yoyo string during a stage performance. Implement the function yoyo(tricks) where the input is a list of integers representing different trick maneuvers. Positive numbers represent clockwise loops that add one unit of string tension. Negative numbers represent counterclockwise loops that remove one unit of tension. If the absolute tension ever exceeds five units, the string knots itself and the performance immediately ends. A trick represented by the number ninety nine signals a manual string adjustment that resets the tension to exactly zero. Return the total number of successfully completed tricks before the end of the list or a knot occurs. For example, given tricks of one, one, and negative one, it returns three.

title: Metronome Tempo Drift
spec: Monitor a wooden mechanical metronome that loses accuracy as its spring unwinds. Define the function tempo(beats) taking a list of measured time intervals between clicks in milliseconds. The target tempo is always defined as the very first interval in the list. As the spring unwinds, intervals naturally lengthen. If an interval is more than twenty milliseconds longer than the target, the metronome is considered drifting. If three consecutive beats drift, the musician winds the key, which resets the next interval to exactly the target tempo, ignoring whatever value was in the input for that specific beat. Return the total number of times the musician had to wind the key. For example, given five hundred followed by four instances of five hundred thirty, it returns one.

title: Neon Sign Flasher
spec: Control a storefront neon sign that has four glass tubes flashing in a sequence. Write the function illuminate(pulses) where the input is a list of integer electrical pulses. A positive pulse turns on the tube corresponding to that number, from one to four. A negative pulse turns that specific tube off. If a pulse is exactly five, it toggles the state of all four tubes simultaneously, turning off those that are on and turning on those that are off. A pulse of zero resets the entire sign, turning all tubes off. Return a list of four integers representing the final state of each tube, using one for on and zero for off. For example, given pulses of one, two, and negative one, it returns zero, one, zero, and zero.

title: Pinball Drop Targets
spec: Calculate the score from a bank of mechanical drop targets in a pinball machine. Create the function pinball(hits) where the input is a list of integers representing the target position hit by the silver ball, from one to five. Knocking down a standing target awards ten points. Hitting a target that is already down awards nothing. If all five targets are successfully knocked down, they instantly reset to the standing position and the player is awarded a fifty point bonus. Return the total accumulated score after all hits in the sequence are processed. For example, given hits of one, two, three, four, and five, it returns one hundred.

title: Slide Rule Alignment
spec: Determine a multiplication result using an analog slide rule simulation. Implement the function calculate(scales) where the input is a list of two integer values representing physical distance markings on a fixed wooden scale and a sliding scale. To simulate the alignment, take the first input value and add it to every multiple of ten from zero up to one hundred. Find the closest absolute match between these generated positions and the second input value. The difference between the closest match and the second value is the margin of error. Return a tuple containing the closest matching position and the margin of error. For example, given scales of five and thirty two, it returns thirty five and three.

title: Sundial Shadow Projector
spec: Track the movement of a shadow across a stone sundial throughout the day. Define the function shadow(hours) taking a list of integers representing solar hours from sunrise to sunset. For each hour strictly before noon, which is represented by twelve, the shadow length decreases by three units. For each hour strictly after noon, the shadow length increases by four units. At exactly noon, the shadow length is zero. If a passing cloud obscures the sun, represented by a negative hour value, the shadow vanishes and its length is recorded as zero for that period. Return a list of the calculated shadow lengths in order. For example, given hours of ten, twelve, and fourteen, it returns six, zero, and eight.

title: Pinhole Camera Exposure
spec: Calculate the required film exposure time for a wooden pinhole camera. Write the function expose(conditions) where the input is a list of integers representing ambient light levels measured every minute. The camera requires a total accumulated light score of exactly or greater than five hundred to fully expose the film. Each minute, the ambient light level is added to the accumulated total. If the light level drops below ten, it is too dim to affect the film and nothing is added to the total for that minute. Once the total reaches five hundred, the shutter is closed. Return the number of minutes the shutter remained open, or negative one if it never reached the required total. For example, given conditions of three hundred and three hundred, it returns two.

title: Anemometer Wind Cups
spec: Measure wind gusts using a mechanical cup anemometer. Create the function wind(speeds) where the input is a list of wind speed measurements in miles per hour. The anemometer only registers a spin if the wind speed is strictly greater than five. Every continuous sequence of speeds above five counts as a single gust event. Find the highest speed recorded within each individual gust event. Return a list of these maximum speeds for every distinct gust event recorded in the input. For example, given speeds of two, ten, twelve, two, and eight, it returns twelve and eight.

title: Boomerang Flight Path
spec: Evaluate the return trajectory of a carved wooden boomerang. Implement the function throw(angles) where the input is a list of integers representing the turning angle at each second of flight. A perfect return requires the sum of all angles to be exactly three hundred and sixty degrees. If the sum exceeds four hundred degrees, the boomerang crashes into the ground. If any single turn angle is negative, it means a sudden gust of wind reversed the flight, invalidating the throw completely. Return one for a perfect return, two for a crash, three for a wind interruption, and zero for an incomplete throw. For example, given angles of ninety, ninety, ninety, and ninety, it returns one.

title: Marionette String Entanglement
spec: Control a wooden marionette puppet and avoid tangling its strings. Define the function puppet(moves) taking a list of integers representing limb movements, where one is the left arm, two is the right arm, three is the left leg, and four is the right leg. Moving the exact same limb three times in a row creates a twist in its string. If any string accumulates two twists, it becomes fully tangled and that limb can no longer move. Subsequent commands for a tangled limb are simply ignored. Return a list of four integers containing the final twist counts for all four strings in numerical order. For example, given moves of one, one, one, and two, it returns one, zero, zero, and zero.

title: Harp String Resonance
spec: Simulate sympathetic resonance in the strings of a concert harp. Write the function pluck(notes) where the input is a list of integers representing plucked string frequencies. When a string is plucked, any other string that is exactly one octave higher, meaning double the frequency, or one octave lower, meaning half the frequency, will also begin to vibrate. This secondary vibration does not cause further cascading resonance. Collect all unique frequencies that vibrate either directly from being plucked or from sympathetic resonance. Return a list of these unique vibrating frequencies sorted from lowest to highest. For example, given notes of four hundred, it returns two hundred, four hundred, and eight hundred.

title: Calligraphy Ink Flow
spec: Model the depletion of ink in a fountain pen during calligraphy. Create the function letter(strokes) where the input is a list of integers representing the pressure applied during each pen stroke. The pen holds a maximum of one hundred units of ink. A stroke consumes ink equal to twice its pressure value. If the pen does not have enough ink to complete a stroke, it uses whatever is left, and the stroke is considered dry. A negative pressure value indicates dipping the pen in the inkwell, which completely refills it to one hundred units. Return the total number of dry strokes encountered. For example, given strokes of sixty and sixty, it returns one.

title: Bookbinding Stitch Planner
spec: Organize loose sheets of paper into stitched signatures for bookbinding. Implement the function bind(pages) where the input is a list of integers representing chapter lengths in pages. A signature is a folded bundle that can hold up to sixteen pages. Sheets are added to the current signature one chapter at a time. If adding a full chapter would exceed the sixteen page limit, the current signature is tied off and a new one is started with that chapter. Any chapter longer than sixteen pages must be split across multiple signatures, filling each to the absolute maximum before continuing. Return the total number of signatures required to bind the entire book. For example, given pages of ten, ten, and twenty, it returns three.
